definition_zh: 监禁；关押；把……投入监狱；使陷于牢笼般的境地
definition_en: to shut a person or animal inside a prison or any place that allows no way out
core_image: 一个人被推进铁栅门内，门闩在他身后落下，外面的路从此不再属于他
scene: 士兵把俘虏带进石墙围起的小院，铁门在身后落锁，街市的声音一下就远了。 The soldiers imprisoned the captured officer in a stone cell behind the walls.
sceneCN: 这里指把人关进监狱，对应第 1 个义项：把某人投入监所；句意为士兵把被俘的军官关在石墙后的牢房里。画面要点：俘虏、石墙小院、从外面落下的门闩。

pos.zh: 监禁；关押（多用于被动，常与 in、for 连用）
禁锢；使如处牢笼（比喻用法）

collocations.phrase: imprison an animal in a cage

derivatives.zh: 监禁；关押（加名词后缀，源自拉丁语，表动作或状态）→ 由「关押」转为「被关押这件事及其状态」
被关押的；受禁锢的（加过去分词词尾，作形容词，表被动状态）→ 由「关押」转为「处在被关押之中的」
可判处监禁的（加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表「能被……」））→ 由「关押」转为「够得上被关押的」
使人如困牢笼的（加现在分词词尾，作形容词，表主动施加）→ 由「关进监狱」转为「在感觉上把人关住的」

senses.title: To put a person into a prison
senses.definition: to confine a person in a prison, especially as a punishment ordered by a court
senses.definitionCN: 把人关押在监狱中，尤指按法庭判决作为惩罚
senses.example: The soldiers imprisoned the captured officer in a stone cell behind the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵把被俘的军官关在石墙后的牢房里。
senses.why: In- carries the meaning 'into' and prison names the place, so the verb says exactly 'to put into a prison'; the core image is a step across a threshold that closes behind.
senses.whyCN: 前缀表示「进入」，prison 指出场所，所以动词说的正是「放进监狱」；核心意象是跨过一道随即在身后关闭的门槛。

senses.title: To hold someone in any closed place
senses.titleCN: 把某人关在任何封闭之处
senses.definition: to keep a person where they cannot leave, even if the place is not a formal prison
senses.definitionCN: 把人留在无法离开的地方，即使那地方并非正式监狱
senses.example: The sailors were imprisoned below deck while the storm lasted.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴期间，水手们被关在甲板下面。
senses.why: Prison had already widened from a building to any act of holding, so the verb can put a person in a cellar or a cabin as long as the way out is shut.
senses.whyCN: prison 早已从建筑物扩大到任何扣留行为，所以只要出口被封住，动词就可以把人关进地窖或船舱。

senses.title: To shut an animal in an enclosure
senses.titleCN: 把动物关进围栏或笼子
senses.definition: to confine an animal in a cage, pen or other enclosure
senses.definitionCN: 把动物关在笼子、围栏或其他封闭处所内
senses.example: The farmer imprisoned the injured bird in a wooden cage until it healed.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫把受伤的鸟关在木笼里，直到它痊愈。
senses.why: The same verb serves any creature that can be shut in; the cage replaces the cell and the species of the prisoner is no part of the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词适用于任何能被关住的生物；笼子替换了牢房，被关者的种类并不参与词义。

senses.title: To hold a suspect before trial
senses.definition: to keep an accused person in custody while the case is still being heard
senses.definitionCN: 在案件仍在审理时把被指控者关押起来
senses.example: Police may imprison a suspect only for a limited period before a hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 警方只能在听证之前有限期地关押嫌疑人。
senses.why: The verb says nothing about a verdict; it only says the door is locked, so it can describe custody imposed while no court has yet spoken.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词不涉及判决，只说明门已锁上，因此可以描述法庭尚未发话时就已实施的羁押。

senses.title: To hold someone without any right to
senses.definition: to confine a person unlawfully, as a kidnapper or an armed group does
senses.definitionCN: 非法地把人关起来，如绑架者或武装团体所为
senses.example: The gang imprisoned the travellers in a cellar for three days.
senses.exampleCN: 那伙人把旅客关在地窖里三天。
senses.why: Because the word describes the lock rather than its legality, a captor with no authority performs the very same action and the same verb applies.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述的是锁，而不是锁是否合法，所以毫无权限的掳掠者做出同一动作时，仍用同一个动词。

senses.title: To confine a mind or a life
senses.definition: to make someone feel trapped by fear, habit or circumstance, without any physical walls
senses.definitionCN: 使人因恐惧、习惯或处境而感到被困住，并无实体的墙
senses.example: Fear of failure had imprisoned her imagination for years.
senses.exampleCN: 对失败的恐惧多年来禁锢着她的想象力。
senses.why: Only the wall needs to be real in the base sense; once fear or routine takes its place, the verb can confine something that cannot be seen at all.
senses.whyCN: 在本义里只有墙必须是真实的；当恐惧或惯例取代了墙，动词就能关住完全看不见的东西。

senses.title: To trap matter inside a solid
senses.titleCN: 把物质封存在固体之内
senses.definition: to hold water, gas or another substance so that it cannot escape from rock or crystal
senses.definitionCN: 使水、气体或其他物质被封在岩石或晶体中而无法逸出
senses.example: Water imprisoned in the rock rises to the surface as a spring.
senses.exampleCN: 封存在岩石中的水以泉水的形式升到地面。
senses.why: Matter can be held the way a person is held: rock that will not let water out is said to imprison it, so the lock is borrowed for the crystal.
senses.whyCN: 物质也能像人一样被留住：不让水逃出的岩石被说成把水关住，锁的意象就此借给了晶体。

senses.title: To hold a whole group at once
senses.definition: to confine many people together in a camp, ghetto or other closed area
senses.definitionCN: 把许多人集中关押在营地、隔离区或其他封闭区域
senses.example: The authorities imprisoned thousands of civilians in the camp.
senses.exampleCN: 当局把数千平民关押在营地里。
senses.why: The verb has no singular subject built into it, so the same act can fall on thousands at once and the camp simply becomes a cell on a larger scale.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词本身不限定单一对象，所以同一动作可一次落在数千人身上，营地只是放大后的牢房。

intro.en: Imprison is formed inside English from in- 'into' and the noun prison. Prison descends through Old French from Latin prehensio 'a seizing', a noun of action from prehendere 'to grasp', so the word began with a hand taking hold of a person. The Latin noun for a prison building, carcer, belongs to another family and plays no part here.
intro.cn: imprison 是在英语内部用表「进入」的前缀与名词 prison 构成的。prison 经古法语上溯拉丁 prehensio「抓取」，那是动词 prehendere「抓住」的动作名词，所以这个词最初是一只手把人拿住。拉丁语中表示监狱建筑的 carcer 属另一词族，与此无关。

items.en: Prehendere meant to seize, grasp or lay hold of; it is attested in classical texts and its principal parts are prehendi and prehensum.
items.cn: prehendere 意为抓住、握取或拿住；古典文献中确有此词，其主要形式为 prehendi 与 prehensum。

items.en: The action noun prehensio named a seizing or a capture, and in later usage it could also mean the keeping of a captive.
items.cn: 动作名词 prehensio 指抓取或捕获，在后来的用法中也可指对俘虏的扣留。

items.en: Old French reduced the Latin noun to prison, which covered both the act of holding and the room where a person was held.
items.cn: 古法语把这一拉丁名词缩略为 prison，兼指扣留行为与关人的处所。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the thirteenth century and used it mainly for the building and for the state of being inside it.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入该词，主要用于指建筑物以及身在其中的状态。

items.en: Adding the prefix that means 'into' produced a verb that could take an object: to put that person into the place. Its early records are medieval and the exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 加上表示「进入」的前缀，便造出可带宾语的动词：把那个人放进那个场所。其早期记录属中世纪，确切年代不确定。

items.en: Later the verb extended to animals in cages, to minds held by fear and to water sealed in rock; the dates of these transfers are uncertain.
items.cn: 后来动词扩展到笼中的动物、被恐惧困住的心智以及封在岩石里的水；这些语义转移发生的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group gathers forms that echo the verb, three from the same Latin capture family and one only resembling it; the second group offers near alternatives for putting a person away.
note.cn: 第一组收与这个动词形近的形式，其中三个同出拉丁「抓取」词族，一个只是形近；第二组是「把人关起来」的近义替代。

entries.definition: The place itself, which supplies the whole second half of the verb; here a building is named, not an action.
entries.definitionCN: 场所本身，构成了这个动词的后半截；此处命名的是建筑，不是动作。

entries.definition: The act of grasping; it keeps the Latin sense of taking hold that the verb inherited.
entries.definitionCN: 抓取的动作；它保留了这个动词所继承的「拿住」本义。

entries.definition: The state or act of being confined, built from this verb with a suffix of action; it names the result rather than the deed.
entries.definitionCN: 被关押的状态或行为，由这个动词加表动作的后缀构成；它命名结果而非动作。

entries.definition: A mark or feeling left by contact; it is merely similar in form and not cognate, being built on a verb meaning 'to press into'.
entries.definitionCN: 接触留下的印记或感觉；只是形近、并非同源，它建于表示「压入」的动词。

entries.definition: To put someone in a local lock-up; it is the everyday word for the same act and carries no hint of the Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人关进地方看守所；它是同一动作的日常说法，不带那层拉丁词根。

entries.definition: To keep within bounds; it works for a room, a bed or a subject, and so is broader and less punitive.
entries.definitionCN: 使留在界限之内；它可用于房间、病床或话题，因此更宽泛、惩罚色彩更淡。

entries.definition: To keep a person in official custody, often briefly; it stresses that release is being withheld.
entries.definitionCN: 把人置于官方扣留之下，往往时间较短；它强调不放人。

entries.definition: To put someone in a jail or camp; it means the same thing but comes from Latin carcer, a wholly different family.
entries.definitionCN: 把人关进监狱或营地；意思相同，却出自拉丁 carcer，属完全不同的词族。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin capture root, the real related forms and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「抓取」词根、真实的同族形式与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Split the word as 'into' plus 'prison', which is how it was actually built.
normal.cn: 把词拆成「进入」加「监狱」，这正是它当初的造法。

normal.en: Prison descends from Latin prehensio 'a seizing', so the word began as a hand closing on someone.
normal.cn: prison 上溯拉丁 prehensio「抓取」，所以这个词最初是一只手把人抓住。

normal.en: Prehendere 'to grasp' also gives prehension and apprehend, both about taking hold.
normal.cn: prehendere「抓住」还给出 prehension 与 apprehend，都与拿住有关。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the legal frame: be imprisoned for, be imprisoned without trial, unlawfully imprison.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法律框架：因……被监禁、未经审判被关押、非法拘禁。

normal.en: The result noun is imprisonment, so a verb that puts a person in becomes a noun for the state of being in.
normal.cn: 结果名词是 imprisonment，于是「把人关进去」的动词变成「处于其中」的名词。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing a man's shoulders through a doorway, then the door closing on the hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把人的肩膀推进门里，随后门在那只手上合拢。

abstract.en: Picture a bird in a cage drawn with the same lines as a cell.
abstract.cn: 想象一只笼中的鸟，笼子的线条与牢房一模一样。

abstract.en: Picture a thought wearing a collar and chain, unable to leave the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一个念头戴着项圈与锁链，走不出房间。

examples.en: The regime imprisoned the editor for a single article.
examples.cn: 该政权因一篇文章就把这位编辑关押起来。

examples.en: Debt had imprisoned him in a job he could not leave.
examples.cn: 债务把他困在一份他离不开的工作里。

examples.en: They imprison the bees in hives during the cold months.
examples.cn: 寒冷月份里，他们把蜜蜂关在蜂箱中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阴森森」：铁门里阴森森的，人被硬推进去就再难出来 → 监禁、关押

root: 拉丁 prehendere「抓住」→ prehensio「抓取、捕获」→ 古法语 prison「扣留；监所」→ 英语 prison；英语在其前加表「进入」的前缀构成 imprison，与 carcer「监狱」无关。

sensesIntro.en: One movement stands behind all eight senses: a person or thing is pushed across a threshold and the way back is shut. That gives the prison, the closed room, the cage, the pre-trial cell, the kidnapper's cellar, the trapped mind, the water sealed in stone, and finally the many behind one camp gate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项背后只有一个动作：人或其他东西被推过一道门槛，回路随即关上。由此依次得到监狱、封闭的房间、兽笼、审判前的牢房、绑架者的地窖、被困住的心智、封在石中的水，最后是同一道营门后的许多人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body pushed through a gate that is then barred from the outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个身体被推过门，随后门从外面闩上。

branches.en: THE DEED AT TWO SCALES: one person put in a cell, or thousands put in a camp.
branches.cn: 两种规模的行为：一人被关进牢房，或数千人被关进营地。

branches.en: ANY ENCLOSURE: a cabin, a cellar or a cage can take the place of the prison.
branches.cn: 任何封闭处所：船舱、地窖或兽笼都能取代监狱。

branches.en: BEFORE THE VERDICT: the door is barred while the case is still open.
branches.cn: 判决之前：案子未结，门已闩上。

branches.en: WITHOUT A RIGHT: the same barred door, held by someone who may not hold it.
branches.cn: 没有权利：同一扇闩上的门，却由无权这样做的人把守。

branches.en: THE THRESHOLD LEAVES THE WORLD: fear walls in a mind, and stone walls in water.
branches.cn: 门槛离开现实世界：恐惧把心智围住，岩石把水围住。

intro.en: The verb is a prefix plus a noun, and both halves are still recognisable in English today.
intro.cn: 这个动词是一个前缀加一个名词，两半在今天仍可辨认。

latinIntro.en: The prefix comes from Latin in- 'into', while the noun descends from prehensio, the action noun of prehendere 'to grasp'.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀出自拉丁语中表「进入」的 in，名词则源自 prehensio，即 prehendere「抓住」的动作名词。

items.example: The prefix supplies the direction of the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀提供动作的方向。

items.meaning: the same prefix, reshaped before a lip sound
items.meaningCN: 同一前缀在双唇音前为顺口而变形的写法
items.example: Before a p the nasal is written as m.
items.exampleCN: 在 p 之前，这个鼻音写作 m。

items.example: The prison stands beside the river.
items.exampleCN: 那座监狱立在河边。

items.example: They imprisoned him for his beliefs.
items.exampleCN: 他们因他的信念把他关押起来。

items.example: The law imprisons no one without a hearing.
items.exampleCN: 法律不会在未经听证的情况下关押任何人。

items.example: The imprisoned poet wrote on scraps of paper.
items.exampleCN: 被关押的诗人在纸片上写作。

items.meaning: the act of confining, or a quality that confines
items.meaningCN: 关押的动作，或使人受困的性质
items.example: The imprisoning heat kept everyone indoors.
items.exampleCN: 令人无处可逃的酷热使所有人都待在室内。

items.example: The court ordered three years of imprisonment.
items.exampleCN: 法庭判处三年监禁。

items.meaning: serious enough for a prison sentence
items.example: The offence is imprisonable under the statute.
items.exampleCN: 按该法规，这项罪行可判处监禁。

definition_zh: 监禁；关押；囚禁；（作为状态的）被收押；刑期；禁锢状态
definition_en: the state of being confined in a prison or jail, or the act of putting a person there
core_image: 铁门在身后合上，长长走廊尽头是一排上锁的牢房，人只能在栅栏后数着日子
scene: 宣判结束后，法警把被告带下法庭台阶，直接押往县看守所那扇厚重的铁门。 After the sentence was read, the marshals took the defendant downstairs for incarceration in the county jail.
sceneCN: 这里指「被收押在监所里、人身自由被剥夺」这一状态，对应第 1 个义项：人已身处牢房之内、不能自行离开；句意为宣判之后，法警把被告带下法庭，送往县看守所关押。画面要点：铁门、长走廊、一排上锁的牢房。

pos.zh: 监禁；关押（多作不可数名词指状态，也可作可数名词指一段关押经历）

derivatives.zh: 由 incarceration 去掉名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作或状态）→ 由「被关押的状态」回到「把人关进牢中」这一动作
incarcerate 加过去分词词尾（转作形容词）→ 由「已被关进去」转为「处于被关押状态的」
拉丁 carcer（牢笼）加形容词后缀→ 由「牢笼」转为「与监狱、监禁制度有关的」
incarceration 与 rate 复合 → 由「监禁」转为「衡量在押人口比例的统计指标」

senses.title: The prison state: held behind bars
senses.titleCN: 被关在铁栏之后的处境
senses.definition: the condition of a person who is confined in a prison or jail and cannot leave by their own will
senses.definitionCN: 被关押在监狱或看守所之内、不能凭自己意愿离开的处境
senses.example: The report described the conditions of incarceration in the old county jail.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了旧县监狱中的关押条件。
senses.why: Latin carcer named a walled pen, and with in- 'into' plus a noun ending for a state, the word settles on being inside that pen rather than on the building that holds it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 carcer 指围起来的圈栏，加上表示「进入」的前缀与表状态的名词后缀，这个词就落在「身处围栏之内」的处境上，而不是指关人的那栋建筑。

senses.title: The act of locking away: the door closing
senses.definition: the act by which an authority places a person in custody in a prison or jail
senses.definitionCN: 有权机关将某人收押进监狱或看守所的行为
senses.example: The law limits the incarceration of juveniles to exceptional cases.
senses.exampleCN: 法律把对未成年人的关押限制在例外情形。
senses.why: The same abstract ending can name either the deed or the condition it produces, so the noun also looks at the instant the key turns, not only at the years that follow.
senses.whyCN: 同一个抽象名词后缀既能指行为，也能指行为造成的结果，因此这个词也会看钥匙转动的那一刻，而不只是之后的漫长年月。

senses.title: Time served: the calendar inside
senses.definition: a length of time that a person spends confined under sentence
senses.definitionCN: 被判刑者在监所内度过的时长
senses.example: He completed a five-year incarceration before returning to his hometown.
senses.exampleCN: 他服完五年刑期后才回到家乡。
senses.why: Once the confined state is measured along a calendar it becomes a block of time, and people speak of serving it, finishing it or having it reduced.
senses.whyCN: 被关押的状态一旦沿着日历被丈量，就变成一段可以「服完」「结束」「缩短」的时间块。

senses.title: Mass incarceration: a social pattern
senses.titleCN: 作为社会现象的大规模监禁
senses.definition: the large-scale and sustained imprisonment of a group or population by a legal system
senses.definitionCN: 某一法律制度对某群体或大量人口长期、成规模地关押
senses.example: Scholars link mass incarceration to changes in sentencing law.
senses.exampleCN: 学者把大规模监禁与量刑法律的变动联系起来。
senses.why: One cell repeated across a whole society stops being a private fate: the same enclosure, multiplied by policy, is read as a pattern of the state.
senses.whyCN: 一间牢房被整个社会重复无数次，就不再是私人命运：同一个围合经政策放大，被读成国家层面的模式。

senses.title: Wrongful incarceration: the key held unjustly
senses.definition: confinement that lacks lawful justification or that later proves to have been unjust
senses.definitionCN: 缺少合法依据、或事后被证明不公正的关押
senses.example: The inquiry documented years of wrongful incarceration.
senses.exampleCN: 调查记录了多年的错误关押。
senses.why: The walls stay exactly the same, but the hand that holds the key is now judged: the noun adds the idea that the enclosure should never have closed.
senses.whyCN: 墙还是同样的墙，但握钥匙的那只手此时受到评判：这个词多出一层「这道门本不该关上」的意思。

senses.title: A cage without bars: figurative confinement
senses.definition: a condition of being shut in or trapped as though inside a cage, without any literal prison
senses.definitionCN: 并无真实监狱、却像被关在笼中一样被禁锢的处境
senses.example: Her illness became an incarceration of the mind as much as of the body.
senses.exampleCN: 她的病既困住了身体，也把心关了起来。
senses.why: The bars need not be iron: any circumstance that removes a person's room to move reproduces the shape of the cell, so the prison word serves as a metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 栏杆不必是铁做的：任何削减一个人活动余地的处境都复制了牢房的形状，于是这个监狱用语被借作比喻。

senses.title: Medical trapping: tissue held fast
senses.definition: in medicine, the trapping of a hernia or an organ in a narrow opening so that it cannot slip back
senses.definitionCN: 医学上疝或器官被卡在狭窄开口中、无法回纳的情形
senses.example: Imaging showed the incarceration of a loop of bowel.
senses.exampleCN: 影像显示一段肠管发生了嵌顿。
senses.why: Clinical language borrowed the prison image for a loop of tissue held where it does not belong, unable to return to its proper place.
senses.whyCN: 临床语言借用了监狱意象，指一段组织被卡在它不该待的位置、回不到原处。

senses.title: A line in the file: recorded legal fact
senses.titleCN: 档案里的一条法律事实
senses.definition: the recorded fact of having been held in custody, counted in law, employment checks and research
senses.definitionCN: 被收押的经历被记录在案，成为法律、雇佣审查与研究统计中的一项事实
senses.example: Applicants are not asked about their incarceration history.
senses.exampleCN: 申请表格不询问申请人的被监禁经历。
senses.why: Modern administration turns the state into a data field: once a jail stay is written down, the noun names a fact about a person's past rather than a place or a moment.
senses.whyCN: 现代行政把这种处境变成一个数据栏：一次关押被写下来之后，这个词指的就是一个人过去的一项事实，而不是某个地点或某个瞬间。

intro.en: Incarceration is built inside Latin: in- 'into' plus carcer 'prison or enclosure' plus -atio, a suffix for an action or its result. English took the finished noun rather than assembling it anew. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: incarceration 是在拉丁语内部构成的：表示「进入」的前缀、意为「牢笼、围栏」的词干，再加表动作或结果的名词后缀；英语是把成品整词接收过来，而不是自己重新拼装。年代均为约数。

items.en: Carcer was the Latin word for a prison, a walled pen and the starting stalls of a circus; the shared idea was an enclosure that holds something in.
items.cn: carcer 是拉丁语中「监狱、围起的圈栏、竞技场出发栅」的说法，共同点是把东西关在里面的围合结构。

items.en: The verb incarcerare added in- 'into' to carcer, so it meant to put a person inside the enclosure.
items.cn: 动词 incarcerare 在 carcer 之前加表示「进入」的成分，意思就是把人送进这个围合之中。

items.en: The abstract noun incarceratio named both the act and the resulting state, and English kept that double reach.
items.cn: 抽象名词 incarceratio 同时指动作与由此形成的状态，英语沿用的正是这种两可的覆盖范围。

items.en: English adopted the noun in the sixteenth century, at first for literal imprisonment under law.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收了这个名词，最初指法律意义上的实际关押。

items.en: Later centuries extended it to mass imprisonment as policy and to the trapping of tissue in medicine.
items.cn: 后世又把它扩展到作为政策的大规模监禁，以及医学上组织被卡住的情形。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin prison stem or merely resembles the word in spelling; the second group offers plainer words for holding a person against their will.
note.cn: 第一组或与本词共享拉丁「牢笼」词干，或只是拼写相近；第二组是「违背意愿留住一个人」的更朴素说法。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to put a person in prison; it is the action behind the noun, not a different family.
entries.definitionCN: 表示把某人关进监狱的动词，是名词背后的动作，并非另一词族。

entries.definition: An adjective built on the Latin prison word, meaning of or relating to prisons and their system.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁「监狱」一词构成的形容词，指与监狱及其制度有关的。

entries.definition: The appearance of a god or an idea in bodily form; it looks close but comes from Latin caro 'flesh', so it is merely look-alike, not a relative.
entries.definitionCN: 神或观念以肉身显现；拼写相近，但出自拉丁 caro「肉」，只是形近，并非同源。

entries.definition: To burn something to ashes; it resembles the word in shape but comes from Latin cinis 'ash', so it is merely look-alike, not a relative.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物烧成灰；拼写相似，但出自拉丁 cinis「灰」，只是形近，并非同源。

entries.definition: The state of being in prison; it is plainer and more neutral than the formal noun.
entries.definitionCN: 在监狱中的状态；比这个正式名词更直白、更中性。

entries.definition: Being kept within limits, whether in a cell, a room or a bed; it need not involve a prison at all.
entries.definitionCN: 被限制在一定范围之内，可以是在牢房、房间或病床上；完全不必涉及监狱。

entries.definition: Being held in official custody, often before trial, with less weight of sentence than incarceration.
entries.definitionCN: 被官方羁押，常在审判之前，量刑意味比监禁弱。

entries.definition: Official keeping of a person by an authority; it names who holds the person rather than the place.
entries.definitionCN: 官方对某人的监管看护；它说的是谁扣着这个人，而不是关在哪里。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin prison word, the real prefix and suffix, and real derived words.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「监狱」一词、真实的前缀与后缀，以及真实的派生词。

normal.en: Carcer is Latin for a prison or a walled pen, so incarceration is literally 'being put into a carcer'.
normal.cn: carcer 在拉丁语里是监狱或围栏，incarceration 字面就是「被放进一个 carcer」。

normal.en: The prefix in- means 'into': the person is placed inside the enclosure, not merely left near it.
normal.cn: 前缀表示「进入」：人被放进围合的内部，而不只是被留在旁边。

normal.en: The ending -ation names an action or a state, which is why the word covers both the locking up and the years after.
normal.cn: 后缀表示动作或状态，因此这个词既覆盖落锁关人，也覆盖之后的年月。

normal.en: The verb incarcerate and the adjective carceral share the stem, so learning one opens the others.
normal.cn: 动词 incarcerate 与形容词 carceral 共用同一词干，记住一个就能带出另一个。

normal.en: Fixed phrases keep the modern sense: mass incarceration, incarceration rate, a term of incarceration.
normal.cn: 固定搭配守住现代义：大规模监禁、监禁率、一段刑期。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy door closing behind you while the corridor lights go out one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇沉重的门在你身后合上，走廊的灯一盏一盏熄灭。

abstract.en: Picture a bird in a cage with the key lying on a table outside the bars.
abstract.cn: 想象笼中有一只鸟，钥匙就放在栏杆外的桌上。

abstract.en: Picture a wall calendar with a cross scratched into it for every day inside.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上挂着一本日历，每过一天就刻下一道叉。

examples.en: The judge reduced the sentence, but incarceration still lasted eleven months.
examples.cn: 法官缩短了刑期，但监禁仍持续了十一个月。

examples.en: Researchers measure incarceration by counting people held on a given day.
examples.cn: 研究人员以某一天的在押人数来衡量监禁规模。

examples.en: Long after release, the years of incarceration still shaped his habits.
examples.cn: 获释很久之后，多年的监禁仍然塑造着他的习惯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬卡塞进」——人被硬卡着塞进铁门里去，门一落锁只剩牢房 → 监禁、关押

root: 拉丁语表「进入」的前缀 + carcer「牢笼、围栏」→ incarcerare「关进牢中」→ incarceratio「关押（动作或状态）」；英语 incarceration 即「被关入牢笼的状态」，同族词有 incarcerate、carceral。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one picture: a body placed inside an enclosure it cannot leave. The noun then reads that enclosure as a state, as an act, as time served, as a social pattern, as an injustice, as a metaphor, as a medical trapping and finally as a recorded legal fact.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都守着同一幅画面：一个人被放进走不出去的围合之中。名词随后把这围合读成状态、读成动作、读成刑期、读成社会模式、读成冤屈、读成比喻、读成医学上的嵌顿，最后读成档案里的一条法律事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing behind a locked cell door, with the corridor outside stretching away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在上锁的牢门之后，外面的走廊一直延伸出去。

branches.en: THE CONDITION: a person is inside the enclosure and cannot leave, which is the plainest reading of the noun.
branches.cn: 处境：人被围在里面、走不出来，这是名词最朴素的读法。

branches.en: THE ACT: the same noun looks at the moment the door is locked and names what the authority does.
branches.cn: 动作：同一个名词也看落锁的那一刻，指权威所做的事。

branches.en: TIME AND INJUSTICE: the state stretched over a calendar becomes a term, and when the key was wrongly held it becomes a grievance.
branches.cn: 时间与冤屈：状态沿日历拉长成刑期；若钥匙本不该被握着，就变成一桩冤屈。

branches.en: SCALE: one cell repeated across a society turns a private fate into a public pattern.
branches.cn: 规模：一间牢房在社会里被重复无数次，私人命运就成了公共模式。

branches.en: OUTSIDE THE PRISON: the cage can be illness, a trapped organ or a line in a file, as long as something is held fast.
branches.cn: 牢房之外：只要有什么被牢牢卡住，笼子就可以是疾病、被嵌顿的器官，或档案里的一行字。

intro.en: The word is assembled from a Latin prefix, a Latin noun stem and a Latin noun suffix; none of the three parts is native English.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁前缀、拉丁名词词干和拉丁名词后缀拼成，三者都不是英语本土成分。

latinIntro.en: Latin carcer 'prison' also yielded the verb incarcerare and the related adjective stem used in English carceral.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 carcer「监狱」还衍生出动词 incarcerare，以及英语 carceral 所用的相关形容词词干。

items.example: The prefix places the person inside the enclosure.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把人放进围合的内部。

items.example: The stem supplies the image of the cage.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供了笼子的意象。

items.meaning: the act of, or the state produced
items.meaningCN: 动作，或动作造成的状态
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a name for what was done and what resulted.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成指「做了什么、落下什么结果」的名词。

items.meaning: the state or act of being imprisoned
items.example: The report measured incarceration in the county.
items.exampleCN: 报告统计了该县的监禁情况。

items.meaning: to put a person into prison
items.example: Courts incarcerate people under sentence.
items.exampleCN: 法院把被判刑的人关进监狱。

items.example: The incarcerated man wrote to his family.
items.exampleCN: 那名被关押的男子给家人写了信。

items.example: Scholars study the carceral system.
items.exampleCN: 学者研究这套监狱制度。

items.meaning: to make; to put into a state
items.example: The ending marks the word as a verb of action.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把该词标为表示动作的动词。

items.meaning: a measure of how many people are imprisoned
items.meaningCN: 衡量在押人口比例的指标
items.example: The incarceration rate rose sharply that decade.
items.exampleCN: 那十年间监禁率急剧上升。

latinEntries.meaning: the starting gates of a circus

definition_zh: 相互的；对等的；有来有往的；倒数（数学）；相互代词（语法）
definition_en: given or done by each of two sides to the other, so that what is received balances what is offered
core_image: 两个人隔着桌子互相递东西，你递过去一份，对方立刻回递同样一份，两只手在同一高度上往返
scene: 两家实验室签下协议，一方开放样本库，另一方回赠测序数据，双方义务一一对应。 The two laboratories signed a reciprocal agreement to share samples and sequencing data.
sceneCN: 两家实验室签订对等协议：一方开放样本库，另一方回赠测序数据，双方义务彼此对应；句中的 reciprocal 指「双方对等互换的」（第 1 个义项：一方给出，另一方以同等之物回报）。图中可辨识物件：两份协议书、来回传递的样本盒、对开的签名页。

pos.zh: 相互的；对等的；互惠的；方向相反的
倒数（数学）；相互代词（语法）

derivatives.zh: 回报；报答；往复运动（加表示动作的动词后缀，使「往复」成为可执行的动作）
报答；互相给予；机械往复（加表示过程的名词后缀，把动作变为过程本身）
互惠；互惠性（加表示性质的抽象名词后缀，把「对等」抽成一种性质）
相互地；对等地（加副词后缀，让对等关系修饰动作方式）
往复式的（现在分词作形容词，指机械沿直线来回）

senses.title: Giving back what is given
senses.definition: given by each side to the other so that what one receives balances what one offers
senses.definitionCN: 一方给出之后，另一方以分量相当之物回赠，使往来两端互相抵消
senses.example: The two universities run a reciprocal exchange of students every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 两所大学每年春天互派学生，往来对等。
senses.why: Latin reciprocus described motion that turns back the way it came, so the oldest sense is a giving that returns to the giver rather than stopping at the receiver.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 reciprocus 描述的是掉头沿原路返回的运动，因此最早的意思是一种回到给出者手里的给予，而不是停在收受者那里。

senses.title: Matching in opposite direction
senses.definition: placed or directed the opposite way so that the two sides correspond exactly
senses.definitionCN: 朝相反方向放置或指向，使两侧恰好一一对应
senses.example: A reciprocal course steers the vessel back along the line it has just followed.
senses.exampleCN: 反向航向把船引回它刚刚走过的那条航线。
senses.why: the idea of turning back is visible here as geometry: two lines run in opposite directions yet answer to each other exactly.
senses.whyCN: 「掉头返回」在这里表现为几何关系：两条线方向相反，却彼此严丝合缝地对应。

senses.title: The number that gives one
senses.definition: the number by which a given number must be multiplied to produce one
senses.definitionCN: 一个数与它相乘恰好得到一时，后者就是前者的倒数
senses.example: The reciprocal of four is one quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 四的倒数是四分之一。
senses.why: a reciprocal value undoes a multiplication, so the term carries the old image of a step that exactly reverses another step.
senses.whyCN: 倒数值能把一次乘法抵消回去，因此这个术语沿用了「一步恰好反转另一步」的旧意象。

senses.title: The pronoun of mutual action
senses.definition: a pronoun such as each other or one another that shows an action passing both ways
senses.definitionCN: 表示动作双向进行的代词，如「彼此」「互相」一类的词
senses.example: In the clause they blamed each other, the pronoun is reciprocal.
senses.exampleCN: 在「他们互相责怪」这一小句中，该代词是相互代词。
senses.why: the grammar label borrows the core image directly: the action leaves one participant, reaches the other, and comes back.
senses.whyCN: 这个语法标签直接借用了核心意象：动作从一方出发，到达另一方，又回到原处。

senses.title: A relation that holds both ways
senses.titleCN: 逻辑与亲属关系中的对称关系
senses.definition: a relation that, whenever it holds between one item and another, also holds in the reverse order
senses.definitionCN: 一种关系，只要甲对乙成立，颠倒过来乙对甲也成立
senses.example: Cousinship is a reciprocal relation, since the reverse of the link always holds too.
senses.exampleCN: 表亲关系是一种对称关系，因为这条连线反过来也永远成立。
senses.why: logic took the everyday notion of a matched return and made it exact: no direction of the relation may be left without its counterpart.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学把日常「对等回报」的观念精确化：关系的任何一个方向都不允许缺少对应的一方。

senses.title: Mutual benefit among organisms
senses.titleCN: 生物学与社会学中的互惠行为
senses.definition: describing behaviour in which help given now is returned later by the receiver
senses.definitionCN: 描述这样一种行为：此刻给出的帮助，日后由受助者回还
senses.example: Grooming among unrelated animals is reciprocal: help given now is returned later.
senses.exampleCN: 无亲缘关系的动物之间的理毛是对等的：此刻给出的帮助日后会被回还。
senses.why: field studies of animals reused the word because the pattern is literally give-and-take deferred in time, not shared possession.
senses.whyCN: 动物行为研究借用了这个词，因为这种模式确实是延后兑现的给与取，而不是共同拥有。

senses.title: Back-and-forth motion
senses.definition: describing motion that repeatedly travels one way and then the opposite way
senses.definitionCN: 描述沿一个方向走完再反向走回、如此反复的运动
senses.example: The pump converts rotary drive into a reciprocal motion of the piston.
senses.exampleCN: 这台泵把旋转驱动转成活塞的往复运动。
senses.why: this is the Latin image in its most physical form: the moving part never settles, because its path is a return.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁意象最物理化的一面：运动部件从不停住，因为它的路径本身就是一次返回。

senses.title: Concessions exchanged in trade
senses.titleCN: 外交与贸易中的互惠减让
senses.definition: describing tariff or market concessions that each country grants in return for those of the other
senses.definitionCN: 指各国彼此给予、以换取对方同等让步的关税或市场减让
senses.example: Both governments offered reciprocal tariff reductions on agricultural machinery.
senses.exampleCN: 两国政府就农业机械互相给予对等的关税减让。
senses.why: diplomacy fixed the word to signed bargains, where every clause granted by one party must be answered by a clause from the other.
senses.whyCN: 外交文书把这个词固定用于签成的交易：一方让出的每一条，都必须由另一方以一条来回应。

intro.en: Reciprocal comes from Latin reciprocus 'returning, alternating, mutual'. Its earlier pre-Latin shape is generally reconstructed as a compound of re- 'back' and pro- 'forward' with an adjectival ending, an image of movement that goes and comes. The deeper origin is uncertain, and the starred form is a reconstruction.
intro.cn: reciprocal 来自拉丁 reciprocus「返回的、交替的、相互的」。其更早的前拉丁形式一般重构为由表示「向后」的拉丁前缀与表示「向前」的拉丁前缀加形容词性后缀构成的复合词，意象是去了又回的往复运动；更深来源不确定，带星号的形式属于重构形式。

items.en: Reciprocus meant 'returning, alternating, mutual'. It described things that move back the way they came, and from that 'alternating' sense it also came to mean 'shared by two sides'.
items.cn: reciprocus 意为「返回的、交替的、相互的」，描述沿原路折返之物；由「交替」这一层，又引申出「双方共有」的意思。

items.en: The pre-Latin form is generally reconstructed as a compound of re- 'backward' and pro- 'forward' plus an adjectival suffix; the pattern of a going and a coming is visible in the two prefixes. This starred form is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 其前拉丁形式一般重构为由表示「向后」的成分与表示「向前」的成分加形容词性后缀构成的复合词，一去一回的格局就写在这两个前缀里；带星号的形式是重构形式，并非有记录的真实词形。

items.en: The verb reciprocare 'to move back and forth, to exchange' grew from the adjective, and English later took it as reciprocate.
items.cn: 动词 reciprocare「来回移动、交换」由该形容词长出，英语后来把它吸收为 reciprocate。

items.en: English adopted reciprocal in the sixteenth century, probably through French, first for things that correspond to each other in opposite directions.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收 reciprocal，可能经由法语，最初用于指方向相反却彼此对应的东西。

items.en: Mathematics fixed the noun sense 'inverse value' by the eighteenth century, grammar named the reciprocal pronoun in the nineteenth, and trade treaties made the adjective standard in the twentieth.
items.cn: 数学在十八世纪固定了「倒数值」的名词义，语法学在十九世纪命名了相互代词，贸易条约则在二十世纪使这个形容词成为标准用语。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of Latin reciprocus is not settled, and any Indo-European root proposed for it beyond the reconstructed compound is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定：拉丁 reciprocus 的更早来源并无定论，在重构复合词之外为它提出的任何印欧词根都只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same Latin family that are easily mistaken for one another; group two holds words about two-way relations, where mutual and reciprocal differ in what they stress.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁词族的各种形式，彼此极易认错；第二组都谈双向关系，其中 mutual 与 reciprocal 的侧重并不相同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to give or feel something in return, or of a machine part to move back and forth; reciprocal is the adjective built on the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指回赠、回应，或指机件往复运动；reciprocal 是由同一词干构成的形容词。

entries.definition: Names the principle or practice of mutual giving; it is the quality, while reciprocal describes a particular arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 指互相给予的原则或做法，是抽象性质；reciprocal 则描述某一具体安排。

entries.definition: Means 'in a mutual way' and modifies a verb; it cannot stand where the adjective is required.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「以相互的方式」，修饰动词，不能放在需要形容词的位置。

entries.definition: The act or process of returning something, or the mechanical stroke that returns; it names an event, not a relation.
entries.definitionCN: 指回赠的行为或过程，也指机械的回程；它命名事件，而非关系。

entries.definition: Stresses something held or felt jointly by both sides, as mutual friends or mutual respect; it does not insist that each side return an equivalent, which reciprocal does.
entries.definitionCN: 强调双方共同拥有或共同感到的东西，如共同的朋友、相互的尊重；它不要求各方回以等量之物，而 reciprocal 有此要求。

entries.definition: Said of agreements or talks involving exactly two parties; it counts the parties, while reciprocal describes the balance of what they exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 指恰好涉及两方的协议或会谈；它数各方数目，而 reciprocal 描述交换是否对等。

entries.definition: Describes two things that fit each other in form or position; it lacks the notion of return or repayment that reciprocal carries.
entries.definitionCN: 指两物在形式或位置上彼此相配；它不含 reciprocal 那种回还与报偿的意味。

entries.definition: Describes parts that complete each other because they differ; reciprocal parts match by returning the same, not by supplying what is missing.
entries.definitionCN: 指因彼此不同而互相补足的部分；reciprocal 的双方靠回以同样的东西相配，而不是靠补上缺口。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here are the real Latin prefixes, the real word family and the real settings in which the word is used.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自这个词真实的拉丁前缀、真实词族，以及它实际出现的场景。

normal.en: re- 'back' plus pro- 'forward': one step out, one step back, and the pair of steps is the meaning.
normal.cn: 表示「向后」的成分加表示「向前」的成分：出去一步、退回一步，这一对步子就是词义。

normal.en: The family runs reciprocal, reciprocate, reciprocation, reciprocity, reciprocally, reciprocating.
normal.cn: 词族包括 reciprocal、reciprocate、reciprocation、reciprocity、reciprocally、reciprocating。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the settings: reciprocal agreement, reciprocal exchange, reciprocal trade, reciprocal altruism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出使用场景：对等协议、对等交换、互惠贸易、互惠利他。

normal.en: Contrast it with mutual: mutual friends are shared, reciprocal favours are returned.
normal.cn: 与 mutual 对照：共同的朋友是共享的，对等的帮助是回还的。

normal.en: Mathematics keeps the noun alive: the reciprocal of four is one quarter.
normal.cn: 数学让名词义继续活着：四的倒数是四分之一。

abstract.en: Picture a tennis rally in which neither player can end the point, because every shot is answered.
abstract.cn: 想象一场网球对拉，谁也结束不了这一分，因为每一拍都被回了过去。

abstract.en: Picture two mirrors facing each other, so each one contains the other without end.
abstract.cn: 想象两面相对而立的镜子，每一面里都装着另一面，无穷无尽。

abstract.en: Picture a handshake held a moment too long, each side waiting for the other to let go.
abstract.cn: 想象一次握得过久的握手，两边都在等对方先松手。

examples.en: Field biologists describe reciprocal grooming as a form of deferred payment.
examples.cn: 野外生物学家把互惠理毛描述为一种延后偿付。

examples.en: The two cities agreed to reciprocal use of their emergency hospitals.
examples.cn: 两座城市同意彼此对等使用对方的急救医院。

examples.en: In any field, the reciprocal of a nonzero element is unique.
examples.cn: 在任何域中，非零元素的倒数是唯一的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞西普若扣」：你扣我一下，我扣你一下，来回对等 → 相互的、对等的、倒数；前缀一去一回的意象可帮助记住「往复」这一核心。

root: 拉丁 reciprocus「返回的、交替的、相互的」→ 前拉丁形式一般重构为 *reco-proco-（由表示「向后」的成分、表示「向前」的成分与形容词性后缀构成）→ 英语 reciprocal；更深来源不确定，带星号者为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: a movement that turns back becomes a giving that is returned, then a structural opposite, an arithmetic inversion, a grammar of mutual action, a symmetric relation, deferred help among organisms, mechanical back-and-forth, and finally signed concessions between states.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线展开：折返的运动先变成回还的给予，再变成结构上的反向对应、算术上的取逆、语法上的互相动作、逻辑上的对称关系、生物间延后兑现的互助、机械的往复，最后落到国家间签成的对等减让。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a step that goes out and comes straight back, so that neither side ends up ahead of the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：迈出一步又原路退回，于是哪一方都不会比另一方多走一截。

branches.en: GIVE AND RETURN: the core movement becomes a balanced exchange, and in space it becomes two directions that answer each other.
branches.cn: 给与回：核心的往复运动先成为均衡的交换，在空间上再成为彼此回应的两个方向。

branches.en: REVERSAL IN LANGUAGE AND NUMBER: multiplication is undone by an inverse value, and an action is undone by turning it back on both participants.
branches.cn: 语言与数目中的反向：乘法被倒数值抵消，动作则被折回两个参与者身上。

branches.en: TWO-WAY STRUCTURE IN RELATIONS AND LIFE: a link that holds both ways, and help that returns after an interval.
branches.cn: 关系与生命中的双向结构：一条正反皆成立的关系，一份隔一段时间又回来的帮助。

branches.en: PHYSICAL STROKE: the same return, now as a piston that must come back before it can go out again.
branches.cn: 物理冲程：同一个「回」，此时表现为活塞必须先退回才能再出去。

branches.en: BARGAINED RETURN: states put the return into writing, so each concession is answered clause by clause.
branches.cn: 写进条款的回：国家把回还固定成文字，于是每一项减让都由另一条条款来回应。

intro.en: The word can be read as two opposed prefixes plus an adjectival ending: a going forward and a coming back, frozen into a quality.
intro.cn: 这个词可以读成两个方向相反的前缀加一个形容词性结尾：一次向前与一次后退，被凝固成一种性质。

latinIntro.en: Latin reciprocus and the verb reciprocare supply the stem; the two prefixes are Latin re- and pro-, and the English endings -ate, -ity and -ally were added later.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 reciprocus 与动词 reciprocare 提供词干；两个前缀分别来自拉丁语的「向后」与「向前」，英语后缀表示动作、性质与方式，都是后来加上的。

items.example: This adjective is the earliest recorded link in the chain.

definition_zh: 可恶的；令人憎恶的；令人反感的；与……相抵触的
definition_en: so hateful or disgusting that one recoils from it, or completely opposed to a principle
core_image: 人看到脏东西时本能地向后退、浑身起鸡皮疙瘩
scene: 档案里记录着看守如何虐待囚犯，读到的人都皱起眉头。 Most readers find the guards' behaviour abhorrent.
sceneCN: 这里 abhorrent 是「令人憎恶的」（第 3 个义项：行为令人强烈反感）；句意为多数读者认为看守的行为令人憎恶。

senses.title: Morally hateful
senses.definition: arousing strong moral disgust and condemnation
senses.definitionCN: 激起强烈的道德厌恶与谴责
senses.example: The exploitation of children is abhorrent.
senses.exampleCN: 剥削儿童是令人憎恶的。
senses.why: Latin abhorrere meant 'to shrink back bristling'; a moral horror repeats the body's instinctive recoil from something unclean.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abhorrere 意为「汗毛竖起地向后退」；道德上的憎恶，重复的正是身体对不洁之物的本能退缩。

senses.title: Revolting to the senses
senses.definition: so foul to smell, taste, or touch that one wants to pull away
senses.definitionCN: 在气味、味道或触感上极其污浊，让人想抽身避开
senses.example: The smell from the drain was abhorrent.
senses.exampleCN: 排水沟里传来的气味令人作呕。
senses.why: The root horrere is about bristling hair, so a stench that makes the skin crawl is the word's most physical use.
senses.whyCN: 词根 horrere 本指毛发竖起，因此让人起鸡皮疙瘩的恶臭是这个词最物理化的用法。

senses.title: Behaviour that disgusts
senses.definition: conduct that viewers or readers find deeply unacceptable
senses.definitionCN: 让旁观者或读者深感无法接受的行为
senses.example: Bullying is abhorrent to most students.
senses.exampleCN: 对多数学生来说，霸凌行为令人反感。
senses.why: Conduct can make observers recoil just as a sight or smell does; the moral audience repeats the physical gesture.
senses.whyCN: 行为也能让旁观者像看到景象或闻到气味那样退缩；道德上的旁观重复了这个身体动作。

senses.title: A crime that shocks
senses.definition: describing an offence whose cruelty causes public horror
senses.definitionCN: 形容残忍程度引发公众恐惧与厌恶的罪行
senses.example: The court condemned the abhorrent crime.
senses.exampleCN: 法院谴责了这起令人发指的罪行。
senses.why: Extreme wrongdoing is pictured as something so foul that the whole community steps back from it.
senses.whyCN: 极端的恶行被想象成极其污浊之物，整个社群都要从它面前退开。

senses.title: Opposed to a principle
senses.definition: completely inconsistent with a rule, value, or principle
senses.definitionCN: 与某项规则、价值或原则完全不一致
senses.example: Such treatment is abhorrent to the principles of the charter.
senses.exampleCN: 这种待遇与宪章的原则相抵触。
senses.why: The 'shrinking back' image turns abstract: a practice and a principle cannot stand together, so the mind recoils from the pairing.
senses.whyCN: 「向后退」的意象转向抽象：一种做法与一项原则无法并存，思维便从这个组合前退开。

senses.title: Contrary to reason
senses.definition: so unreasonable that it cannot be accepted by an ordinary mind
senses.definitionCN: 极度不合情理，普通人的理智无法接受
senses.example: It is abhorrent to reason to punish the victim.
senses.exampleCN: 惩罚受害者与常理不相容。
senses.why: Reason itself is treated as a standard a person can recoil from violating.
senses.whyCN: 理智本身被当作一条标准，人一旦违背它就会本能地退缩。

senses.title: An unacceptable system
senses.definition: describing an institution or practice that a society rejects as unjust
senses.definitionCN: 形容被社会视为不义而拒绝接受的制度或做法
senses.example: The old segregation laws were abhorrent.
senses.exampleCN: 旧的种族隔离法律令人无法接受。
senses.why: Institutions are judged by the same gut reaction once reserved for foul sights and smells.
senses.whyCN: 人们用曾经只针对污浊景象与气味的本能反应，来评判制度。

senses.title: An attitude one rejects
senses.definition: describing a view or attitude that decent people refuse to hold
senses.definitionCN: 形容正派人不愿持有的观点或态度
senses.example: She called the remarks abhorrent and demanded an apology.
senses.exampleCN: 她称这些言论令人憎恶，并要求道歉。
senses.why: Words and attitudes can also carry contamination; the listener pulls back as if from something dirty.
senses.whyCN: 言辞与态度也会带着污浊；听者像避开脏东西一样向后退。

intro.en: Abhorrent comes from a Latin verb for shrinking back with bristling hair, which also gave English horror.
intro.cn: abhorrent 来自一个表示「汗毛竖起、向后退」的拉丁语动词，英语 horror 也由它而来。

items.en: The root *ghers- is reconstructed with the sense 'to bristle'; the link to Latin horrere is generally accepted but not certain in every detail.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *ghers- 被重构为「毛发竖起」之义；它与拉丁语 horrere 的联系一般被接受，但细节并非全部确定。

items.en: horrere meant 'to bristle, tremble, shudder', and it is the source of horror.
items.cn: horrere 意为「毛发竖起、发抖、战栗」，是 horror 的来源。

items.en: ab- 'away' plus horrere formed abhorrere, 'to shrink back from with horror'.
items.cn: ab-（离开）与 horrere 构成 abhorrere，意为「因恐惧而向后退避」。

items.en: The present participle abhorrens, 'shrinking back from', is the direct model of the English adjective.
items.cn: 现在分词 abhorrens 意为「对……退缩的」，是英语形容词的直接模型。

items.en: English formed abhorrent from the Latin participle, first in the sense of physical recoil.
items.cn: 英语由这个拉丁语分词构成 abhorrent，最初表示身体上的退缩。

items.en: The moral sense broadened until anything hateful, and later anything inconsistent with a principle, could be called abhorrent.
items.cn: 道德义不断扩展，直到任何可恨之事、后来任何与原则不符之事，都可以被称为 abhorrent。

note.en: The first group gathers the verb, the noun, and the adverb from the same family; the second gathers adjectives of strong dislike.
note.cn: 第一组收同族的动词、名词与副词；第二组收表示强烈厌恶的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun meaning intense disgust and hatred.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「憎恶、厌恶」，指强烈的反感与痛恨。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to hate something deeply.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「憎恶、痛恨」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'in a hateful or disgusting way'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「令人憎恶地」。

entries.definition: The noun for a feeling of fear and revulsion, from the same bristling root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「恐惧、惊恐」，与 abhorrent 共享表示毛发竖起的词根。

entries.definition: Extremely distasteful or unacceptable, often to a moral sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人反感的」，常指道德上难以接受。

entries.definition: Deserving strong dislike; thoroughly hateful.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可憎的」，指理应受到强烈厌恶。

entries.definition: Causing disgust, especially something foul or diseased.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人作呕的」，尤指污浊或病态之物。

entries.definition: Deserving contempt because of low or cruel behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「卑鄙的、可鄙的」，因行为卑劣残忍而应受蔑视。

entries.definition: Extremely unpleasant and causing a strong physical reaction.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人作呕的」，指极度不快并引发强烈生理反应。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Latin root shared with horror and the fixed 'abhorrent to' pattern; the abstract hooks picture the recoil itself.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用与 horror 共享的拉丁词根和固定的 abhorrent to 结构；抽象记忆点想象退缩的动作。

normal.en: Abhorrent and horror share the Latin root for bristling hair; horror is the feeling, abhorrent is what causes it.
normal.cn: abhorrent 与 horror 共享表示毛发竖起的拉丁词根；horror 是感受，abhorrent 是引起感受的东西。

normal.en: Abhorrent to is the fixed pattern for something inconsistent with a principle.
normal.cn: abhorrent to 是固定结构，表示与某项原则不相容。

normal.en: Abhor is the verb, abhorrence the noun, abhorrent the adjective.
normal.cn: 动词是 abhor，名词是 abhorrence，形容词是 abhorrent。

normal.en: Morally abhorrent is a frequent pairing in news and commentary.
normal.cn: morally abhorrent 是新闻与评论中的高频搭配。

normal.en: The -ent ending marks a present participle, so abhorrent is literally 'shrinking back'.
normal.cn: -ent 结尾标明现在分词，所以 abhorrent 字面就是「正在退缩的」。

abstract.en: Picture a person stepping back and covering the nose at a filthy smell.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人闻到污浊气味，后退一步并捂住鼻子。

abstract.en: Picture hair standing up on the back of a neck in sudden disgust.
abstract.cn: 想象一阵突来的厌恶让后颈的汗毛竖起。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd turning away from a cruel act as if from a bad smell.
abstract.cn: 想象人群像避开恶臭一样，从残忍行为前转过身去。

examples.en: Racism is abhorrent to any fair society.
examples.cn: 种族主义与任何公平社会都格格不入。

examples.en: The idea of selling the school was abhorrent to parents.
examples.cn: 卖掉这所学校的想法让家长们无法接受。

examples.en: He found the cruelty of the experiment abhorrent.
examples.cn: 他觉得这项实验的残忍令人憎恶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿伯恨他」——阿伯一看见那人做的事就浑身发冷、连连后退，恨得不愿靠近。

root: 拉丁语 ab-（离开）+ horrere（毛发竖起、发抖），构成 abhorrere（因恐惧而退缩）；核心义是「一见就起鸡皮疙瘩地退开」

sensesIntro.en: The senses begin with physical revulsion and moral disgust, then extend to behaviour, crime, institutions, and ideas that conflict with principle.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从生理上的作呕与道德厌恶开始，再扩展到行为、罪行、制度，以及与原则冲突的观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body stepping back with hair standing on end
core.cn: 核心意象：汗毛竖起、身体向后退的一步

branches.en: Physical and moral disgust: the body and the conscience both recoil.
branches.cn: 生理与道德的厌恶：身体与良知同时退缩。

branches.en: People and their words become revolting to the audience.
branches.cn: 人及其言辞让受众产生强烈反感。

branches.en: Crimes and institutions are condemned as foul and unacceptable.
branches.cn: 罪行与制度被谴责为污浊、不可接受。

branches.en: The recoil turns abstract: a practice conflicts with a principle or with reason.
branches.cn: 退缩转向抽象：做法与原则或理智发生冲突。

branches.en: The fixed phrase abhorrent to marks that conflict grammatically.
branches.cn: 固定短语 abhorrent to 在语法上标出这种冲突。

intro.en: The family is built from the Latin stem hor r-, the prefix ab-, and the adjective and noun endings -ent, -ence, and -ly.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁词干 horr-、前缀 ab-，以及形容词与名词后缀 -ent、-ence、-ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin horrere is the shared source of horror, horrid, and abhorrent, so the Latin entries record the verb and its participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 horrere 是 horror、horrid 与 abhorrent 的共同来源，因此拉丁条目记录动词及其分词。

definition_zh: 丧失；损失；亏损；死亡；减少
definition_en: the fact of no longer having something, the money lost in business, or a decrease in amount
core_image: 一只抽屉被拉开，原本放手表的位置空着，只剩一圈浅浅的印痕
scene: 抽屉被拉开，原本放手表的格子空着，只留下一圈浅浅的印痕。 The loss of the old workshop hit the village harder than anyone expected.
sceneCN: 抽屉里原本放手表的位置空着，只剩印痕；句中的 loss 指「不再拥有某物这一事实」（第 1 个义项：失去占有或拥有）。图中可辨识物件：拉开的抽屉、空表位、圆形印痕、旧钥匙、灰尘；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 丧失；损失；亏损；死亡

senses.title: No longer having something
senses.definition: the fact or experience of no longer having something that one had
senses.definitionCN: 不再拥有曾经拥有之物的这一事实或经历
senses.example: The loss of the old workshop hit the village harder than anyone expected.
senses.exampleCN: 老作坊的失去对村庄的打击比任何人预想的都重。
senses.why: The word names the state left behind when a possession or condition is no longer there.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指某物或某种状态不在之后留下的那个空缺状态。

senses.title: A person or thing that is missed
senses.titleCN: 被怀念、被惋惜的人或物
senses.definition: a person or thing whose absence is felt as a deprivation by a group
senses.definitionCN: 其缺席被群体感受为缺失的人或物
senses.example: The retired teacher was a great loss to the school.
senses.exampleCN: 这位退休教师对学校是一大损失。
senses.why: Instead of the event of losing, the word can name the thing whose absence is felt.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以不指「失去」这件事，而指那个缺席被感受到的人或物。

senses.title: Money lost in business
senses.definition: the amount by which spending exceeds income in a business or year
senses.definitionCN: 企业或年度中支出超过收入的金额
senses.example: The airline reported a loss for the third year running.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司连续第三年报告亏损。
senses.why: Accounting reverses the idea of gain: what should have come back did not, and the shortfall is the loss.
senses.whyCN: 会计把收益的观念反过来：本该回来的没有回来，缺掉的那部分就是亏损。

senses.title: The death of someone close
senses.definition: the death of a relative or friend, experienced as bereavement
senses.definitionCN: 亲属或朋友的死亡，被视为丧亲之痛
senses.example: She took a long leave after the loss of her father.
senses.exampleCN: 父亲去世后，她请了很长的假。
senses.why: Death is the most absolute form of no longer having someone, so the word serves as its ordinary, gentle name.
senses.whyCN: 死亡是「不再拥有某人」最绝对的形式，因此这个词成了它平常而温和的说法。

senses.title: A decrease in amount or intensity
senses.definition: a reduction in quantity, energy or intensity as something escapes or fades
senses.definitionCN: 随着某物逸出或衰减，数量、能量或强度上的减少
senses.example: Insulation cut heat loss through the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 保温层减少了穿过墙壁的热量散失。
senses.why: Physics treats escaping heat as something that leaves the system, which is a loss to the system.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把逸出的热视为离开系统的某物，对系统而言就是损失。

senses.title: Failure to win a contest
senses.definition: a defeat in a game, election or contest
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、选举或竞争中落败
senses.example: It was their third loss of the season.
senses.exampleCN: 这是他们本赛季的第三场失利。
senses.why: A defeat is the loss of a winning position, and sport shortened the phrase to the single word.
senses.whyCN: 失败就是失去获胜的位置，体育语境把这个短语缩短成一个词。

senses.title: An insured event or sum
senses.titleCN: 保险中的损失事件或金额
senses.definition: the damage or sum that an insurer agrees to cover under a policy
senses.definitionCN: 承保人依保单同意赔付的损害或金额
senses.example: The policy covered the loss of the cargo at sea.
senses.exampleCN: 保单承保了海上货物的损失。
senses.why: Insurance exists to price misfortune, so the word becomes a technical term for the event and its cost.
senses.whyCN: 保险的存在就是为不幸定价，因此这个词成了指事件及其代价的技术用语。

senses.title: The gap left by something valuable
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：珍贵之物消失后留下的空缺
senses.definition: the emptiness or deficit that remains after something valuable disappears
senses.definitionCN: 珍贵之物消失之后留下的空虚或欠缺
senses.example: The loss of trust was harder to repair than the loss of money.
senses.exampleCN: 信任的丧失比金钱的损失更难修补。
senses.why: Generalised, the word names any absence that registers as a deficit, whether the thing was money, heat, a person or trust.
senses.whyCN: 一般化之后，这个词指任何被感受为欠缺的缺席，无论所失之物是金钱、热量、人还是信任。

intro.en: Loss comes from Old English los 'loss, destruction', from a Germanic stem also seen in the verb lose; it has no Latin cognate. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: loss 来自古英语 los「丧失、毁灭」，其日耳曼语词干也见于动词 lose；这个词没有拉丁同族词。年代为约数。

items.en: The noun goes back to a Germanic form meaning 'breaking up, loss', related to Old Norse los 'the breaking up of an army'.
items.cn: 这个名词可追溯到日耳曼语中表示「瓦解、丧失」的形式，与古诺尔斯语 los「军队溃散」相关。

items.en: Old English los meant 'loss, destruction, ruin', and the related verb losian meant 'to be lost, perish'.
items.cn: 古英语 los 意为「丧失、毁灭、毁坏」，相关动词 losian 意为「失踪、灭亡」。

items.en: In Middle English the noun settled into its modern spelling and the verb separated into lose, so the pair now differ in form and sound.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，名词固定为现代拼写，动词则分立为 lose，于是这对词在形与音上都分开了。

items.en: The commercial sense of a shortfall in the accounts developed in the sixteenth century alongside double-entry bookkeeping.
items.cn: 账目中出现缺口的商业义在十六世纪随复式记账一同发展。

items.en: Insurance made the word a term for a covered event, and sport made it a count of defeats; both usages spread in the modern period.
items.cn: 保险使这个词成为「承保事件」的术语，体育使它成为失败次数的计量；两种用法都在近代普及。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed, and the exact dates of the financial and insurance senses are not established.
items.cn: 来源不确定：更早的印欧词根属重构形式，财务义与保险义的确切年代亦未得到证明。

note.en: Group one holds the forms of the same Germanic stock, including one that drifted to a different meaning; group two holds words for damage, shortfall and defeat.
note.cn: 第一组同出日耳曼语词干，其中一个漂移到了别的意思；第二组指损害、缺口与失败。

entries.definition: To stop having something; the noun names the state, the verb names the event, and their spellings must not be swapped.
entries.definitionCN: 失去某物；名词指状态，动词指事件，两者的拼写不可混用。

entries.definition: The past participle and an adjective meaning missing or unable to find the way.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，也作形容词，意为丢失的或迷路的。

entries.definition: A person who loses, especially one who fails to win; it names a person, not an amount.
entries.definitionCN: 指失败的人，尤指未能获胜者；指人而非金额。

entries.definition: From the same Germanic root meaning 'free, loose', but it means 'not tight' and is not a synonym of loss.
entries.definitionCN: 同出表示「自由、松开」的日耳曼词根，但意为「不紧的」，并非 loss 的同义词。

entries.definition: Harm to a thing that reduces its value or usefulness; loss is the value that is gone.
entries.definitionCN: 对物品造成的损害，降低其价值或用途；loss 指已经失去的价值。

entries.definition: The amount by which something falls short, especially in public accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 某物不足的数额，尤指公共账目中的缺口。

entries.definition: A gradual decrease in amount or quality; it describes a process, while loss can be a single event.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或质量的逐渐下降；描述过程，而 loss 可以是一次事件。

entries.definition: The state of being beaten in a battle, game or election; it is narrower than loss.
entries.definitionCN: 在战斗、比赛或选举中被击败的状态；比 loss 更窄。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Germanic history, the real family and the real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的日耳曼语演变、真实词族与真实搭配。

normal.en: The old noun meant 'breaking up': something that was whole is now apart or gone.
normal.cn: 这个旧名词意为「瓦解」：原本完整的东西现在散开或消失了。

normal.en: The family runs lose, lost, loser, loss, lossless, lossy.
normal.cn: 词族包括 lose、lost、loser、loss、lossless、lossy。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: at a loss, make a loss, cut losses, weight loss.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义：困惑或亏本、亏损、及时止损、体重下降。

normal.en: Loss is the state; lose is the event.
normal.cn: loss 是状态，lose 是事件。

normal.en: Accounting sets loss against profit, and sport sets it against a win.
normal.cn: 会计把亏损与利润相对，体育把失利与胜利相对。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer with one empty slot where something used to sit every day.
abstract.cn: 想象一只抽屉，其中一个格子空了，那里原本每天都放着东西。

abstract.en: Picture a wall that lets warmth escape through it all winter.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙，整个冬天都让暖意从里面溜走。

abstract.en: Picture a column in a ledger that should have a number and has none.
abstract.cn: 想象账簿里一栏本该有数字，却空着。

examples.en: The loss of the harvest left the family short of cash.
examples.cn: 收成的损失让这家人现金短缺。

examples.en: Insurers estimate the loss before they settle the claim.
examples.cn: 承保人在理赔之前先估算损失。

examples.en: The team never recovered from that early loss.
examples.cn: 这支队伍始终没能从赛季初的那场失利中恢复过来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「落了（loss）就找不回」——东西掉了、钱亏了、人走了，都叫丧失

root: 古英语 los（丧失、毁灭），属日耳曼语源，与动词 lose 同出一系；更早的印欧词根属重构形式，无拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one absence: something that was there is no longer, and the word then names the thing missed, the money short, a death, an escaping quantity, a defeat, an insured event and finally any deficit at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个缺席展开：原本在那里的东西不在了；这个词再指被惋惜的对象、账上的缺款、死亡、逸出的量、一场失利、承保事件，最后指任何欠缺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty place in a drawer where something used to be.
core.cn: 核心意象：抽屉里一个原本放着东西的空位。

branches.en: ABSENCE: the event of losing and the thing whose absence is felt are two sides of one empty place.
branches.cn: 缺席：失去的事件与缺席被感受的对象，是同一个空位的两面。

branches.en: ACCOUNTS: the money that should have come back did not, and the gap is counted as a loss.
branches.cn: 账目：本该回来的钱没有回来，这个缺口就被计为亏损。

branches.en: DEATH: the most absolute absence gets the gentlest name.
branches.cn: 死亡：最绝对的缺席用了最温和的名称。

branches.en: MEASURED ABSENCE: escaping heat and insured cargo are both quantities that leave and must be priced.
branches.cn: 可量的缺席：逸出的热与承保的货物，都是离开并被定价的量。

branches.en: CONTEST AND GENERALITY: a defeat is the loss of a winning position, and any deficit repeats the same shape.
branches.cn: 竞争与泛化：失利是失去获胜位置，任何欠缺都重复同一形状。

intro.en: Loss is a native Germanic noun with no prefix and no Latin root; its ending marks a state rather than an act.
intro.cn: loss 是本族日耳曼名词，既无前缀也无拉丁词根；其词尾标记一种状态，而非一个动作。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor here; the Germanic noun los and the verb lose supply the whole family, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语祖先；日耳曼名词 los 与动词 lose 提供整个词族，因此拉丁词条留空。
