senses.title: The activity of working with computers
senses.titleCN: 使用计算机干活这件事
senses.definition: the activity of working with computers to store, analyse or present information
senses.definitionCN: 使用计算机存储、分析或呈现信息的活动
senses.example: Daily computing in the newsroom means editing copy and checking feeds.
senses.exampleCN: 新闻编辑室每天的计算机工作就是改稿和查信息流。
senses.why: The verbal noun -ing names an activity rather than a device, so the word covers the whole of what people do with machines.
senses.whyCN: 动名词 -ing 命名一种活动而非一台设备，因此这个词覆盖人们用机器做的一整套事情。

senses.title: The academic discipline
senses.definition: the academic field that studies algorithms, software, systems and the theory behind them
senses.definitionCN: 研究算法、软件、系统及其背后理论的学科领域
senses.example: She chose computing as her major because she liked logic more than code.
senses.exampleCN: 她选了计算专业，因为她更喜欢逻辑而不是写代码。
senses.why: A department needs a name for the field, and the activity word is broad enough to hold theory, engineering and applications together.
senses.whyCN: 院系总得给学科一个名字，而表示活动的词足够宽，能把理论、工程与应用都装进去。

senses.title: The processing a machine performs
senses.definition: the operations a machine carries out on data, considered as a process rather than a product
senses.definitionCN: 机器对数据执行的一系列操作，看重过程而非产物
senses.example: The chip does all the computing locally instead of sending it to a distant server.
senses.exampleCN: 芯片在本地完成全部计算，而不是把计算送到远处的服务器。
senses.why: When attention shifts from the machine to what happens inside it, the -ing noun names the processing itself.
senses.whyCN: 当注意力从机器转到机器内部发生的事，-ing 名词就用来指处理本身。

senses.title: Power and resources for calculation
senses.titleCN: 用于计算的算力与资源
senses.definition: the processing power, storage and time that an institution has to buy or allocate
senses.definitionCN: 机构需要采购或分配的算力、存储与机时
senses.example: The budget for computing doubled once the models grew.
senses.exampleCN: 模型变大之后，计算资源的预算翻了一倍。
senses.why: In laboratories and companies the activity becomes a line in a budget, so the mass noun comes to mean the capacity itself.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室与公司里，这项活动会变成预算里的一行，于是不可数名词转而指这份能力。

senses.title: Calculation spread across many machines
senses.titleCN: 分散在许多机器上的计算
senses.definition: the model in which processing and storage are supplied over a network by remote or pooled machines
senses.definitionCN: 通过网络由远程或池化的机器提供处理与存储的模式
senses.example: Cloud computing moved the whole archive off the office machines.
senses.exampleCN: 云计算把整个档案库从办公室的机器上搬走了。
senses.why: Once computing can be rented from a distance, the -ing word attaches to the delivery model rather than to any one device.
senses.whyCN: 当计算可以从远处租用，这个 -ing 词就挂到交付模式上，而不属于任何一台具体设备。

senses.title: Reckoning by hand, the older sense
senses.definition: the older sense of calculation itself, especially arithmetic done with counters, tables or written figures
senses.definitionCN: 指计算本身的旧义，尤指用算筹、表格或纸面数字做的算术
senses.example: Medieval computing meant long division done with counters on a board.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的「计算」指的是在板上用算筹做长除法。
senses.why: Before machines existed, the -ing form simply named the human work of reckoning, and that sense survives in historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 机器出现之前，-ing 形式只表示人做核算这件事，这个义项仍留在历史叙述里。

senses.title: Calculation built into everyday objects
senses.titleCN: 装进日常物件里的计算
senses.definition: the processing embedded in lifts, cars, appliances and sensors, running without a visible screen
senses.definitionCN: 嵌在电梯、汽车、家电与传感器里的处理，不需要可见屏幕也在运行
senses.example: Embedded computing now runs lifts, kettles and door locks.
senses.exampleCN: 嵌入式计算如今在管理电梯、水壶和门锁。
senses.why: When processing disappears into ordinary objects, the activity word is the natural label for something nobody sees.
senses.whyCN: 当处理隐入寻常物件，表示活动的词就成了这种看不见之物的自然标签。

senses.title: The industry that sells calculation
senses.definition: the sector of companies and jobs that build, run or sell computer systems and services
senses.definitionCN: 建造、运营或出售计算机系统与服务的公司与岗位所构成的部门
senses.example: Employment in computing grew faster than in manufacturing.
senses.exampleCN: 计算行业的就业增长快于制造业。
senses.why: An activity sustained by firms turns into an industry, and English happily uses the -ing noun for the sector as well.
senses.whyCN: 由公司维持的活动会变成一个行业，英语也乐于用这个 -ing 名词指整个部门。

intro.en: Computing is the English verbal noun of compute, formed with -ing; compute itself comes from Latin computare 'to reckon together'. The word named arithmetic long before it named the use of electronic machines, and only in the mid-twentieth century did it become the name of a field. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: computing 是 compute 的英语动名词，由 -ing 构成；compute 出自拉丁 computare「一起核算」。这个词先指算术，很久以后才指使用电子机器，直到二十世纪中叶才成为学科名称。年代均为约数。

items.en: Putare 'to reckon, think' is the root verb; repute, dispute and impute belong to the same family.
items.cn: putare「核算、思考」是根动词；repute、dispute 与 impute 属于同一族。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus putare gave computare, 'to reckon together', the source of the English verb compute.
items.cn: com-「一起」加 putare 构成 computare「合起来核算」，是英语动词 compute 的来源。

items.en: Compute entered English in the seventeenth century as a learned verb for reckoning, often in astronomy and navigation.
items.cn: compute 在十七世纪作为书面动词进入英语，表示核算，常用于天文与航海。

items.en: English turns verbs into activity nouns with -ing, so computing first meant the act of reckoning, with no machine in sight.
items.cn: 英语用 -ing 把动词变成活动名词，于是 computing 最初只表示核算这个动作，与机器无关。

items.en: In the 1940s and 1950s the activity moved onto electronic machines, and computing began to mean work done with them.
items.cn: 二十世纪四五十年代，这项活动转移到电子机器上，computing 开始表示用机器完成的工作。

items.en: University departments adopted computing as a field name after the war, and the late twentieth century added cloud computing and distributed computing; first citation uncertain: the precise first academic use of the field name is not settled.
items.cn: 战后大学院系采用 computing 作为学科名，二十世纪末又添上云计算与分布式计算；首见年代不确定：这一学科名最早的学术书证尚无定论。

note.en: Group one is the compute family, where -ing marks the activity while the other forms mark the device, the adjective or the possibility; group two holds words for calculation and for the organised use of data.
note.cn: 第一组是 compute 词族，-ing 标记活动，其余形式分别标记设备、形容词或可能性；第二组是表示计算以及有组织地使用数据的词。

entries.definition: To work out a result by calculation; the activity noun is simply its -ing form.
entries.definitionCN: 通过计算得出结果；活动名词就是它的 -ing 形式。

entries.definition: The countable machine; it answers 'what do you use', not 'what are you doing'.
entries.definitionCN: 可数的机器；回答「你用什么」，而不是「你在做什么」。

entries.definition: Describing methods or costs that belong to calculation, never naming the activity as a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 形容属于计算的方法或代价，从不用作活动的主语。

entries.definition: Said of a task a procedure can in principle finish, a property rather than an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指程序原则上能完成的任务，是一种属性而非活动。

entries.definition: The process of getting a number by arithmetic; it keeps the arithmetic focus without the machines.
entries.definitionCN: 用算术得出一个数的过程；保留算术焦点，不涉及机器。

entries.definition: The branch of mathematics dealing with numbers and basic operations, close to the old sense of computing.
entries.definitionCN: 处理数字与基本运算的数学分支，接近 computing 的旧义。

entries.definition: The study of information systems and their use, often a European name for applied computing.
entries.definitionCN: 研究信息系统及其使用，常是欧洲对应用计算的称呼。

entries.definition: The replacement of human work by machines, which computing makes possible but does not itself name.
entries.definitionCN: 用机器取代人力的过程，computing 使之成为可能，但并不直接指它。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the -ing activity noun, the shift from hand arithmetic to machines, and the field that grew out of it.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：-ing 活动名词、从手工算术到机器的转移，以及由此长出的学科。

normal.en: Compute plus -ing: the doing, not the thing.
normal.cn: compute 加 -ing：是「做」，不是「物」。

normal.en: The word is uncountable, so it never takes a plural.
normal.cn: 这个词不可数，因此没有复数。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: cloud computing, distributed computing, computing power.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：云计算、分布式计算、算力。

normal.en: Schools and departments use it as the name of a field.
normal.cn: 学校和院系用它作为学科名称。

normal.en: Before machines, it meant arithmetic done by hand.
normal.cn: 在机器之前，它指手工做的算术。

abstract.en: Picture a hand moving counters on a board, then the same movement repeating inside a chip.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在板上移动算筹，然后同样的动作在芯片里反复发生。

abstract.en: Picture work that used to fill a room now arriving over a cable from somewhere else.
abstract.cn: 想象曾经占满一间屋的工作，如今顺着一条线缆从别处送过来。

abstract.en: Picture a kettle, a lift and a lock each quietly doing sums of their own.
abstract.cn: 想象水壶、电梯和门锁各自安静地做着自己的算术。

examples.en: Computing has changed what a small team can finish in one week.
examples.cn: 计算改变了小团队一周能完成的事情。

examples.en: The department teaches computing alongside mathematics and design.
examples.cn: 这个院系把计算与数学、设计一起教。

examples.en: Cheap computing made the old simulation routine available to students.
examples.cn: 廉价的算力让学生也能跑起过去那套模拟流程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「com（一起）+ put（放）+ ing（进行）」——把数字放在一起算的这个过程：计算

root: compute 的英语动名词，-ing 构成活动名词；compute 出自拉丁 computare「一起核算」= com-「一起」+ putare「核算」。同根词有 computer、computation、computational。先指手工算术，二十世纪中叶起指使用电子机器的活动与学科。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one activity: daily work with machines, the academic field, the processing inside a machine, the power bought for it, calculation spread over a network, hand reckoning, processing hidden in objects and the industry that sells it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一项活动：日常用机器干活、学科本身、机器内部的处理、为它采购的算力、散布在网络上的计算、手工核算、藏进物件里的处理，以及出售它的行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the act of reckoning, carried out first by hand and later by machines.
core.cn: 核心意象：核算这个动作，先由人手工完成，后来交由机器完成。

branches.en: THE SAME ACT, TWO ERAS: working at a screen today and moving counters on a board long ago are one activity with different tools.
branches.cn: 同一动作，两个时代：今天在屏幕前工作，与很久以前在板上移算筹，是同一项活动换了工具。

branches.en: FROM ACTIVITY TO INSTITUTION: what people do becomes a department, and departments become an industry.
branches.cn: 从活动到建制：人们做的事变成一个院系，院系又变成一个行业。

branches.en: THE INSIDE VIEW: the word can name the operations themselves, not only the work around them.
branches.cn: 内部视角：这个词也能指那些操作本身，而不只是围绕它们的劳动。

branches.en: METERED AND DISTRIBUTED: capacity becomes something bought, and then something delivered from elsewhere.
branches.cn: 可计量且可分发：算力先变成可采购之物，再变成从别处送来的服务。

branches.en: INVISIBLE EVERYWHERE: processing disappears into lifts and locks, where no screen marks it.
branches.cn: 无处不在却看不见：处理隐入电梯与门锁，那里没有屏幕标记它。

intro.en: Computing is a Latin root wrapped in an English verb ending and then turned into an activity noun; each layer also builds other words.
intro.cn: computing 是一个拉丁词根套上英语动词词尾、再转为活动名词的结果，每一层也都参与构造别的词。

latinIntro.en: Com- 'together' plus putare 'to reckon' make computare, which gives compute, computation and computer; English -ing then makes the activity noun from the verb.
latinIntro.cn: com-「一起」与 putare「核算」构成 computare，进而给出 compute、computation 与 computer；英语的 -ing 再从动词造出活动名词。

items.example: The prefix joins separate figures into one reckoning.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把分开的数字并进同一次核算。

items.example: The root covers counting and judging at once.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根同时涵盖计数与判断。

items.example: The Latin verb is the ancestor of every English form here.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词是这里所有英语形式的祖先。

items.meaning: the act or process of doing
items.example: The suffix turns a verb into the name of an activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成活动的名称。

items.example: The machine can compute the sum instantly.
items.exampleCN: 机器能立刻算出这个和。

items.example: The computation filled the whole afternoon.
items.exampleCN: 这次计算占满了整个下午。

items.example: Computing is uncountable in this sense.
items.exampleCN: 在这个义项里它是不可数名词。

items.example: The suffix first meant a person, then a device.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀先指人，后指装置。

items.example: The adjective describes the method rather than the machine.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述方法而非机器。

items.example: The task is computationally cheap.
items.exampleCN: 这项任务在计算上开销很小。

definition_zh: 飞行，飞行的动作；航班，一次空中旅程；飞行的鸟群；一段楼梯；逃跑；飞行轨迹与箭羽
definition_en: the act of moving through the air, and any single instance, group, or path of such movement, including a set of stairs and the feathers that steady an arrow
core_image: 一只鸟从石阶底部掠起，沿着一道弧线飞过屋顶，翅尖的羽毛在光里闪了一下
scene: 清晨的山脊上，一群候鸟被光线的变化惊起，贴着坡面滑向另一侧谷地。 The flock rose into flight as the sun broke over the ridge.
sceneCN: 这里 flight 是「飞行」（第 1 个义项：在空中移动这一动作本身）；句意为太阳越过山脊时，鸟群起飞了。

pos.zh: 飞行；航班；鸟群；一段楼梯；逃跑（可数，复数 flights）
（鸟类）成群飞；给箭装尾羽（较少用，多作专业动词）

forms.label: 派生形容词（装有箭羽的）

senses.title: The Act of Flying
senses.definition: the action or process of moving through the air on wings or in an aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 凭借翅膀或飞行器在空中移动的动作或过程
senses.example: The gulls' flight over the harbour lasted only a few seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 海鸥掠过港湾的飞行只持续了几秒钟。
senses.why: flyht is the bare action noun built on the verb fleogan 'to fly'; the suffix -t turns the doing into a thing you can name.
senses.whyCN: flyht 是由动词 fleogan「飞」直接构成的动作名词，后缀 -t 把「做」变成可以命名的「事」。

senses.title: A Scheduled Air Journey
senses.definition: a trip made by air, especially one operated on a regular service between two places
senses.definitionCN: 乘飞机的一次行程，尤指两地间按班期运营的航次
senses.example: Our flight to Denver leaves before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 我们飞往丹佛的航班在黎明前起飞。
senses.why: a scheduled service is one completed act of flying, so the uncountable action is counted out into separate items.
senses.whyCN: 一次班期服务就是一整次完成的飞行，于是不可数的动作被切分成一个个可数的班次。

senses.title: A Flock on the Wing
senses.definition: a group of birds or aircraft moving through the air together
senses.definitionCN: 一起在空中移动的一群鸟或飞行器
senses.example: A flight of geese crossed the marsh at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 一群大雁在黄昏时飞越沼泽。
senses.why: the collective noun applies the action to the whole body that performs it at one time, so the group is named after its flight.
senses.whyCN: 这个集合名词把动作归给同时做出它的整个群体，于是这一群就以「飞行」命名。

senses.title: A Set of Stairs
senses.definition: a continuous run of steps between one floor or landing and the next
senses.definitionCN: 两层楼或两个平台之间连续的一串台阶
senses.example: She carried the box up the last flight of stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 她把箱子搬上了最后一段楼梯。
senses.why: a run of steps rises step after step like a body climbing through air, so English lent the word for flying to this rising series.
senses.whyCN: 一串台阶一级接一级地上升，像身体在空中爬升，英语于是把「飞行」这个词借给了这道上升的序列。

senses.title: Escape by Running
senses.definition: the act of fleeing or being driven away from danger
senses.definitionCN: 逃离危险或被赶离现场的行为
senses.example: The intruders were put to flight by a single shout.
senses.exampleCN: 一声喊叫就把闯入者赶跑了。
senses.why: fleeing is the oldest figurative use of flying: the body takes off as if on wings, so the same noun covers panic movement on the ground.
senses.whyCN: 逃跑是「飞」最古老的比喻用法：身体仿佛长了翅膀般离开，同一个名词因此也指地面上的仓皇移动。

senses.title: Path of a Projectile
senses.definition: the curved course followed by an arrow, bullet or ball through the air
senses.definitionCN: 箭、子弹或球在空中划出的弧线路径
senses.example: The arrow's flight flattened as it lost speed.
senses.exampleCN: 箭在速度衰减时，飞行弧线变得平缓。
senses.why: a projectile repeats the core action without wings: it too crosses the air along a line, and the line is named after the crossing.
senses.whyCN: 抛射体没有翅膀却重复了核心动作：它也沿一条线穿过空气，这条线就以「穿越」命名。

senses.title: Flight of Fancy
senses.definition: a burst of imaginative invention that has little grounding in fact
senses.definitionCN: 一段缺少事实依据的想象性发挥
senses.example: The plan was a flight of fancy that no budget could support.
senses.exampleCN: 那项计划纯属异想天开，没有哪份预算支撑得起。
senses.why: the mind is pictured as taking off and leaving the ground of fact, exactly the movement the word already names.
senses.whyCN: 这里把心智想象成起飞、离开事实的地面，正是这个词本已命名的那个动作。

senses.title: Feathers on an Arrow
senses.definition: the feathers fitted near the head of an arrow shaft to keep it steady in flight
senses.definitionCN: 装在箭杆尾端附近、使箭飞行稳定的羽毛
senses.example: He replaced the torn flight on the arrow before the match.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛前他换掉了箭上破损的箭羽。
senses.why: the feather is the part that makes the arrow fly straight, so the effect is named by the very act it serves.
senses.whyCN: 羽毛正是让箭飞得笔直的那一部分，于是这一部件用它服务的那个动作来命名。

intro.en: Flight comes straight from Old English flyht, an action noun made from the strong verb fleogan 'to fly' plus the suffix -t. The family is Germanic, not Latin.
intro.cn: flight 直接来自古英语 flyht，是由强动词 fleogan「飞」加后缀 -t 构成的动作名词；整个词族属日耳曼语，与拉丁语无关。

items.en: Fleogan was the everyday verb 'to fly', a strong verb of the second class, and it is the direct ancestor of modern fly.
items.cn: fleogan 是日常表示「飞」的动词，属第二类强动词，是现代 fly 的直接祖先。

items.en: Old English formed action nouns by adding -t to a verb stem, as in gift from giefan and weight from wegan; flyht follows the same pattern.
items.cn: 古英语在动词词干后加 -t 构成动作名词，如 gift 来自 giefan、weight 来自 wegan；flyht 遵循同一模式。

items.en: Flyht meant both the act of flying and a flying group, and it already carried the sense of fleeing from an enemy.
items.cn: flyht 既指飞行的动作，也指飞行的群体，并且已经带有「逃避敌人」的意思。

items.en: Middle English flight kept the noun while the verb became fly; the staircase sense appears in the record later, formed on the image of a rising run of steps.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了名词 flight，动词则演变为 fly；楼梯义在文献中出现较晚，建立在「一级级上升」的意象上。

items.en: German Flug 'flight' and Dutch vlucht are built from the same verb with the same suffix, which confirms the pattern rather than any Latin source.
items.cn: 德语 Flug「飞行」与荷兰语 vlucht 由同一动词加同一后缀构成，这证实了该构词模式，而非任何拉丁来源。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Germanic only): the deeper Indo-European root behind fleogan is a reconstruction, and the arrow-feather sense has no firm first date.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅限日耳曼语之前）：fleogan 背后更早的印欧词根属重构形式，箭羽义的可靠首见年代亦不可考。

note.en: Group one holds words that resemble flight in spelling or sound but mostly belong to other roots; group two holds the travel and airborne words that overlap with one or another of its senses.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写或读音近似、但多数属于其他词根的词；第二组是在某个义项上与 flight 重叠的旅行与空中词汇。

entries.definition: Sudden fear; from Old English fyrhto, a noun of fear, with no connection to flying and no shared root with flight.
entries.definitionCN: 指突如其来的恐惧；来自古英语 fyrhto「恐惧」，与飞行无关，也与 flight 不同词根。

entries.definition: A group of ships, from Old English flēot, tied to flēotan 'to float'; the adjective fleet 'fast' is a separate Norse borrowing, so neither is kin to flight.
entries.definitionCN: 指船队，来自古英语 flēot，与 flēotan「漂浮」相关；形容词 fleet「快速」另从古诺斯语借入，二者都不是 flight 的同源词。

entries.definition: Built on flight plus -y, originally 'given to flight', hence fickle or frivolous; it shares the root but describes temperament.
entries.definitionCN: 由 flight 加 -y 构成，本义为「爱飞的」，引申为轻浮善变；词根相同，但描述的是性情。

entries.definition: To grow feathers fit for flight, from Old English -flycge 'fit to fly'; it belongs to the same flying family, though the exact link to fleogan is not settled.
entries.definitionCN: 指长出适合飞行的羽毛，来自古英语 -flycge「适合飞的」；属于同一「飞」词族，但它与 fleogan 的确切关系尚无定论。

entries.definition: A travel from one place to another by any means; flight is one kind of journey, limited to the air and to a single scheduled leg.
entries.definitionCN: 指以任何方式从一地到另一地的旅行；flight 是其中一种，限于空中且指单个航段。

entries.definition: A long journey, especially by sea or into space; it stresses distance and endurance rather than the act of flying.
entries.definitionCN: 指长途旅行，尤指海上或太空航行；强调距离与耐力，而非飞行动作。

entries.definition: To fly without flapping, riding rising air; it names one style of flight rather than flight as a category.
entries.definitionCN: 指不扇翅、借上升气流滑翔高飞；它命名的是飞行的一种方式，而非飞行这个类别。

entries.definition: The act of getting free from confinement or danger; it overlaps with flight in the sense of fleeing but says nothing about wings.
entries.definitionCN: 指摆脱拘禁或危险；在「逃跑」义上与 flight 重叠，但不含翅膀的意象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real cognates and real idioms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的同源词与真实习语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: fleogan 'to fly' + -t: the act noun is built straight from the verb, exactly as gift is built on give.
normal.cn: fleogan「飞」+ -t：动作名词直接从动词构成，正如 gift 由 give 构成。

normal.en: German Flug and Dutch vlucht repeat the same verb-plus-suffix pattern, which fixes the shape of the word.
normal.cn: 德语 Flug 与荷兰语 vlucht 重复了同一套「动词加后缀」的模式，固定了这个词的形状。

normal.en: The staircase sense keeps the shape of the core image: a series climbing, step after step.
normal.cn: 楼梯义保留了核心意象的形状：一级接一级地向上攀升。

normal.en: put to flight means to make someone fly away, and take flight means to leave the ground or to run.
normal.cn: put to flight 意为使人飞逃，take flight 意为离地起飞或逃走。

normal.en: The family runs fly, flight, flighty, flightless, flighted.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 fly、flight、flighty、flightless、flighted。

abstract.en: Picture a spiral staircase seen from above: each step is one beat of a wing.
abstract.cn: 想象从上方俯瞰一道螺旋楼梯：每一级台阶就是一次振翅。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow's feather slicing the air, correcting the shaft with every wobble.
abstract.cn: 想象箭尾的羽毛切开空气，每一次晃动都被它矫正。

abstract.en: Picture a line of geese at dusk, one continuous stroke drawn across the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏时一列大雁，在天幕上画出一道连续的笔画。

examples.en: The engineer traced the flight of the ball with a slow-motion camera.
examples.cn: 工程师用慢动作摄影机追踪球的飞行轨迹。

examples.en: Bad weather forced the airline to cancel every flight before noon.
examples.cn: 恶劣天气迫使航空公司在中午前取消了所有航班。

examples.en: A flight of swallows passed low over the harvested field.
examples.cn: 一群燕子低低掠过收割后的田野。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「弗莱特」——像滑过天空的一道亮线，一掠而过 → 飞行；再想那段楼梯，也是一级级往上「飞」。

root: 古英语 flyht「飞行、飞行的群体」，由 fleogan「飞」（现代 fly 的祖先）+ 动作名词后缀 -t 构成，日耳曼语族，与德语 Flug、荷兰语 vlucht 同型；fleogan 更早的印欧词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses hang on one movement: something leaves the ground and travels a line through air. Counting that movement gives a flight number, grouping it gives a flock, copying it on the ground gives stairs, fleeing gives escape, and the line it draws gives the trajectory and the feather that steadies it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都挂在同一个动作上：某物离地，在空中走出一条线。把这一动作计数，就有航班号；把做出它的群体归拢，就有鸟群；让它在土地上复制，就有楼梯；用它来逃离，就有逃跑；把那条线取下来，就有弹道，也有让箭沿线的箭羽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body leaving the ground and drawing a line through the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个身体离地，在空中划出一道线。

branches.en: THE ACTION ITSELF: flying, then one finished act of it counted as a scheduled trip.
branches.cn: 动作本身：先有飞行，再把一次完成的飞行计作一个班次。

branches.en: WHAT CARRIES THE MOTION: the flock that flies and the feather that keeps the arrow flying true.
branches.cn: 承载动作之物：飞行的鸟群，以及让箭飞直的羽毛。

branches.en: RISING IN PLACE: a run of steps repeats the climb without any air.
branches.cn: 原地上升：一串台阶在没有空气的地方重复了攀爬。

branches.en: FLYING AWAY: panic turns the same noun into escape.
branches.cn: 飞离：惊慌把同一个名词变成逃跑。

branches.en: THE DRAWN LINE: a projectile follows it literally, a daydream follows it in the mind.
branches.cn: 画出的线：抛射体在实处沿着它，白日梦在心上沿着它。

intro.en: Flight reads as two pieces: the Germanic verb stem for flying, and an old action-noun suffix. Everything else in the family is built by adding English endings to this noun.
intro.cn: flight 可以拆成两段：表「飞」的日耳曼动词词干，以及一个古老的动作名词后缀；词族中其余的词都是在这个名词上再加英语词尾构成的。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin entry to give: flight is Germanic throughout, and its cognates are German Flug and Dutch vlucht, not any Latin noun.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词形可列：flight 全程属日耳曼语，同源词是德语 Flug 与荷兰语 vlucht，而非任何拉丁名词。

items.structure: fleogan (Old English strong verb, class II)
items.meaning: to move through the air on wings
items.example: The stem supplies the bare act of flying.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供「飞」这一纯粹的动作。

items.structure: -t (Old English action-noun suffix, as in gift, weight)
items.meaning: the act or result of doing the verb
items.meaningCN: 动词所指动作或其结果
items.example: Add -t to the verb and the flying becomes a thing.
items.exampleCN: 在动词后加 -t，飞行就变成一件可以指称的事。

items.meaning: the act of flying; a flying group; a fleeing
items.example: Flight is recorded in Old English as flyht.
items.exampleCN: flight 在古英语中写作 flyht。

items.meaningCN: 爱飞的，引申为轻浮善变的
items.example: A flighty person is one whose attention keeps taking off.
items.exampleCN: flighty 的人，注意力总在起飞。

items.example: A flighted arrow carries its own stabiliser.
items.exampleCN: 装有箭羽的箭自带稳定器。

items.example: The suffix removes exactly the capacity the noun names.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀恰好去掉了名词所指的那种能力。

items.meaning: the route or line along which something flies
items.example: Controllers cleared the aircraft along a new flight path.
items.exampleCN: 管制员让这架飞机沿一条新飞行路线通行。

items.meaning: the cockpit, or the deck where aircraft take off
items.example: The flight deck is the part of the ship given to flying.
items.exampleCN: 飞行甲板是舰上专门交给飞行使用的那部分。

items.example: The missile was destroyed in flight.
items.exampleCN: 导弹在飞行途中被摧毁。

definition_zh: 保存；保护；维持；果酱；自然保护区；专属领域
definition_en: to keep something in its original state, or to protect it from harm or change
core_image: 一排玻璃罐把夏天的果子封在糖水里，罐外的果园已经落光了叶子
scene: 果园早已光秃，玻璃罐却把夏天的收成保存了下来。 Glass jars preserve the summer harvest long after the orchard is bare.
sceneCN: 这里 preserve 指「用糖或盐把食物处理过，使其长期不坏」（第 5 个义项：以糖渍、腌渍等方式保存食物）；句意为果园早已光秃，玻璃罐仍封着夏天的收成。图中可辨识物件：玻璃罐、糖汁、果块、贴着手写日期的标签；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 保存；保护；维持；腌制（食物）
蜜饯；果酱（常用复数）；自然保护区；专属领域

senses.title: Keep something from decaying
senses.definition: to treat or store something so that it does not decay
senses.definitionCN: 通过处理或存放使某物不腐坏
senses.example: Salt and smoke preserve meat through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 盐与烟熏能让肉在整个冬天不坏。
senses.why: prae- 'before' plus servare 'keep' gives 'keep beforehand', and keeping food before it spoils is the oldest use of the word.
senses.whyCN: prae-「在前」加 servare「守住」得到「提前守住」，在食物变坏之前先护住，正是这个词最古老的用法。

senses.title: Protect a place from destruction
senses.titleCN: 保护地点、建筑不遭破坏或改造
senses.definition: to protect a building, place or object from being destroyed or altered
senses.definitionCN: 保护建筑、地点或物件不被摧毁或改动
senses.example: The trust preserves the medieval bridge exactly as it stands.
senses.exampleCN: 该信托机构让这座中世纪桥原样留存。
senses.why: the object sense keeps the core meaning untouched: what is preserved is not repaired into something new but kept as it was.
senses.whyCN: 物件义保持了核心含义：被 preserve 的不是被修成新东西，而是按原样留住。

senses.title: Keep a state or quality in being
senses.titleCN: 维持某种状态或品质继续存在
senses.definition: to keep a condition, quality or state continuing
senses.definitionCN: 使某种状况、品质或状态持续下去
senses.example: Officers preserved order while the crowd pushed forward.
senses.exampleCN: 人群向前涌时，警员维持着秩序。
senses.why: order is something that disappears unless it is actively kept, so the verb is used for conditions that need guarding.
senses.whyCN: 秩序若不主动守住就会消失，因此这个词也用于需要守护的状态。

senses.title: Keep something for later generations
senses.titleCN: 为后世留存记录或实物
senses.definition: to keep records, objects or knowledge so that people in the future can still use them
senses.definitionCN: 保存记录、实物或知识，使后人仍能使用
senses.example: Archivists preserve recordings of dialects that no longer have young speakers.
senses.exampleCN: 档案人员保存那些已无年轻使用者的方言录音。
senses.why: here the word looks forward: what is kept now is kept for a time the keeper will never see.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词朝向未来：此刻守住的东西，是为守者永远看不到的时代而留。

senses.title: Prepare fruit or meat with sugar or brine
senses.titleCN: 用糖渍、盐腌等方式加工食物
senses.definition: to prepare fruit or other food with sugar, salt or vinegar so that it keeps
senses.definitionCN: 用糖、盐或醋处理水果等食物以延长保存期
senses.example: Glass jars preserve the summer harvest long after the orchard is bare.
senses.exampleCN: 果园早已光秃，玻璃罐仍封着夏天的收成。
senses.why: the cooking sense specializes the general one: sugar and salt are the agents that do the guarding.
senses.whyCN: 烹调用法是一般义的具体化：糖与盐就是执行「守住」的媒介。

senses.title: A protected area of land
senses.definition: an area of land set aside so that its wildlife or landscape is protected
senses.definitionCN: 为保护野生生物或景观而划出的土地
senses.example: The marsh is a private preserve where hunting is banned.
senses.exampleCN: 这片沼泽是私人保护区，禁止狩猎。
senses.why: the noun turns the act into a place: land where protection happens all the time.
senses.whyCN: 名词义把动作变成地点：持续进行保护的那片土地。

senses.title: Fruit jam in a jar
senses.titleCN: 果酱、蜜饯（美式常用复数）
senses.definition: fruit cooked with sugar and stored in jars
senses.definitionCN: 加糖熬煮后装罐的水果制品
senses.example: She opened a jar of strawberry preserves for the toast.
senses.exampleCN: 她开了一罐草莓酱配吐司。
senses.why: the product noun is inherited straight from the verb, and American English prefers the plural for the jars on the shelf.
senses.whyCN: 成品名词直接承自动词，美式英语更常用复数指架上的那些罐子。

senses.title: An activity reserved for one group
senses.titleCN: 某一群体独占的领域或活动
senses.definition: an activity or area that one group keeps for itself and others are shut out of
senses.definitionCN: 某一群体留给自己、他人不得进入的活动或领域
senses.example: Editing the paper is no longer a male preserve.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑这家报纸不再是男性的专属领域。
senses.why: the idea of keeping something safe for oneself shades easily into keeping others out, which is how this social sense arose.
senses.whyCN: 把某物为自己守住，很容易滑向把别人挡在外面，这个社会义就是这样产生的。

intro.en: Preserve comes through Old French from Latin praeservare, built on prae- 'before' and servare 'to keep'. It shares its root with conserve but not its prefix. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: preserve 经古法语来自拉丁 praeservare，由 prae-「在前」与 servare「守住」构成。它与 conserve 共享词根，但前缀不同。年代均为约数。

items.en: Prae- meant 'before, in front of', and in compounds it often adds the idea of doing something in advance.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前、在……之前」，在复合词中常添「预先」的意思。

items.en: Praeservare meant 'to keep or guard beforehand', a combination of the prefix with servare 'to keep safe'.
items.cn: praeservare 意为「提前看守、预先保住」，是前缀与 servare「守住」的组合。

items.en: Old French preserver brought the word into English in the fourteenth century, and the spelling settled as preserve.
items.cn: 古法语 preserver 在 14 世纪把词带入英语，拼写最终固定为 preserve。

items.en: The food sense is recorded from the sixteenth century; the sense of land set aside for wildlife developed in the nineteenth, when the first large reserves were mapped.
items.cn: 食物义在 16 世纪有记录；为野生生物划出土地的意思在 19 世纪形成，当时最早的几处大型保护区被勘定。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest citation for the jam noun and for the nature-reserve sense is not precisely recorded, and the pre-Latin origin of servare remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：果酱名词义与自然保护区义的最早书证没有确切记录；servare 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds verbs that share the Latin -serve stock and are easily mistaken; group two holds words that also mean keeping something safe but differ in emphasis.
note.cn: 第一组是共享拉丁 -serve 词干、容易认错的动词；第二组同样表示「保住」，但侧重点不同。

entries.definition: Com- plus servare stresses keeping a resource from being used up; preserve stresses keeping something from changing or spoiling.
entries.definitionCN: com- 加 servare 强调不让资源被用尽；preserve 强调不让某物改变或变坏。

entries.definition: Re- 'back' plus servare: to set something aside instead of using it now, as in reserve a table.
entries.definitionCN: re-「向后」加 servare：把某物留到以后再用，如预订餐桌。

entries.definition: Ob- 'toward' plus servare: to watch, notice, or follow a rule; nothing is being stored.
entries.definitionCN: ob-「朝向」加 servare：观看、察觉或遵守规则；并不涉及储存。

entries.definition: De- 'fully' plus servire 'to serve': to have earned something. Same look, different root.
entries.definitionCN: de-「完全」加 servire「服侍」：因服务而应得。形似而词根不同。

entries.definition: To keep something safe from active harm; it says nothing about keeping it unchanged.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物免受主动伤害；不涉及保持原样。

entries.definition: To keep something one already has, such as heat or a right, without the idea of guarding it.
entries.definitionCN: 指继续保有已拥有之物，如热量或权利，不含守护之意。

entries.definition: To use a resource sparingly so that it lasts; its focus is quantity, not condition.
entries.definitionCN: 节制使用资源使其持久；关注的是数量而非状态。

entries.definition: To keep something working by servicing it, as a machine; preserve does not imply repair.
entries.definitionCN: 通过保养使某物继续运转，如机器；preserve 不含修理之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: prae- 'before' + servare 'keep': guard it before harm arrives.
normal.cn: prae-「在前」+ servare「守住」：在伤害到来之前先护住。

normal.en: The family runs preserve, preservation, preservative, preserver, preservationist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 preserve、preservation、preservative、preserver、preservationist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: preserve food, preserve order, nature preserve, fruit preserves.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：保存食物、维持秩序、自然保护区、果酱。

normal.en: The root is shared with conserve and reserve, but the prefixes do the dividing.
normal.cn: 词根与 conserve、reserve 共享，靠前缀区分。

normal.en: American English says preserves for jam, British English often says jam.
normal.cn: 美式英语用 preserves 指果酱，英式英语常用 jam。

abstract.en: Picture a jar of summer standing on a shelf in January.
abstract.cn: 想象一月的架子上摆着一罐夏天。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge left exactly as it was, weeds and all.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥连杂草都原样留着。

abstract.en: Picture a fence that keeps a meadow for animals and people out of it.
abstract.cn: 想象一道篱笆把草场留给动物，把人挡在外面。

examples.en: The museum preserves the letters in acid-free boxes.
examples.cn: 博物馆把信件放在无酸盒中保存。

examples.en: Freezing preserves the flavour far better than drying.
examples.cn: 冷冻保存风味远胜于干燥。

examples.en: The old quarter is preserved as a living neighbourhood, not a museum.
examples.cn: 这片老城区是作为活着的社区被保护，而不是当成博物馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pre（提前）+ serve（守住）」——在坏掉之前先护住 → 保存、保护、维持

root: 拉丁 praeservare「提前守住」= prae-（在前）+ servare「看守、保存」；与 conserve 共享 servare 词根，靠前缀区分。英语 preserve。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: something is guarded before harm reaches it, and that guard is then applied to food, buildings, order, records, land, jam and finally to a social boundary.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：在损害到达之前先护住某物，这道防护再依次用于食物、建筑、秩序、记录、土地、果酱，最后用于一条社会边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a jar and a fence, both keeping something whole against time.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只罐与一道篱笆，都在对抗时间地把某物完整留住。

branches.en: STOP DECAY: sugar, salt and smoke are the guard, whether in a pot or a jar.
branches.cn: 止住腐坏：糖、盐与烟就是那道防护，无论在锅里还是罐里。

branches.en: UNCHANGED OBJECT: a building is kept as it stands, not restored into something new.
branches.cn: 原样的物件：建筑按现状留住，而不是修成新东西。

branches.en: STATE AND RECORD: order and archives both vanish unless someone keeps them.
branches.cn: 状态与记录：秩序与档案若无人守护都会消失。

branches.en: SET ASIDE: the act becomes a place, and the product becomes a jar.
branches.cn: 留出：动作变成一片地，成品变成一罐酱。

branches.en: KEPT FOR SOME: guarding something for oneself ends by shutting others out.
branches.cn: 为某些人留住：为自己守住，最终把别人挡在外面。

intro.en: Preserve is a Latin verb of prefix plus root; the same two parts build conserve, reserve and observe, so the family is best read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: preserve 是由前缀加词根构成的拉丁动词；同样的两部分也构成 conserve、reserve 与 observe，因此这个词族最好按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae- 'before' and servare 'to keep' give praeservare; English draws preserve, preservation, preservative and preserver from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 prae-「在前」与 servare「守住」构成 praeservare；英语由此得到 preserve、preservation、preservative 与 preserver。

items.example: The prefix marks action taken ahead of time.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记提前采取的行动。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of guarding.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供「守护」的意思。

items.example: Salt preserves the fish before it spoils.
items.exampleCN: 盐在鱼变坏之前先把它保住。

items.example: Cold storage aids the preservation of vaccines.
items.exampleCN: 冷藏有助于疫苗的保存。

items.meaning: a substance that keeps food from spoiling
items.meaningCN: 防止食物变坏的添加物
items.example: The label lists no preservatives.
items.exampleCN: 标签上未列出任何防腐剂。

items.meaning: a person or thing that preserves
items.example: He was a preserver of local songs.
items.exampleCN: 他是当地歌谣的保存者。

items.example: Dried grain is preservable for years.
items.exampleCN: 干燥的谷物可保存多年。

items.meaning: an advocate of protecting old buildings or land
items.meaningCN: 主张保护老建筑或土地的人
items.example: Preservationists fought the demolition.
items.exampleCN: 保护主义者反对这次拆除。

items.example: They reserved two rooms for the wedding.
items.exampleCN: 他们为婚礼留了两间房。

latinEntries.meaning: to keep beforehand, protect in advance

definition_zh: 方式；模式；交通方式；生产方式；时尚；调式；语气；众数
definition_en: a way in which something is done, operates, or exists; also a prevailing fashion, a musical scale, a grammatical mood, or the most frequent value in a set
core_image: 一把尺子量出恰好的一段，再照这个尺寸去做
scene: 出行方案表里列了地铁、公交、骑车和步行四种方式，让人比较城市负担得起哪一种。 The transport plan lists four modes — metro, bus, bicycle and walking — and asks which one the city can afford.
sceneCN: 这里 mode 是「交通方式」（第 3 个义项：交通方式）；句意：这份交通规划列出四种方式——地铁、公交、自行车和步行——并追问这座城市负担得起哪一种。场景要点：一张摊开的城市交通图、四条并排的路线、被圈出的预算数字；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 方式；模式；样式；调式；语气；众数

senses.title: A way of doing
senses.definition: the particular way in which someone does something or something happens
senses.definitionCN: 某人做某事或某事发生的特定方式
senses.example: Her mode of working is to write everything by hand before typing it.
senses.exampleCN: 她的工作方式是先把一切手写下来，再打字。
senses.why: Latin modus is a measure. A way of doing something is the measure the action is cut to, so the word begins as the shape given to an activity rather than its purpose.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 modus 是“尺度”。做某事的方式，就是动作被裁成的尺寸，因此这个词的起点是给一项活动定形，而不是给它定目的。

senses.title: A machine setting
senses.definition: one of the fixed settings in which a machine or system can operate
senses.definitionCN: 机器或系统可以运行的固定设置之一
senses.example: At ten the alarm switches itself into night mode.
senses.exampleCN: 到了十点，警报器会自动切换到夜间模式。
senses.why: A machine repeats the same operations, and each setting is a measure it can be set to. The word moves from human ways of acting to the repeatable ways a device acts.
senses.whyCN: 机器重复同样的操作，每一种设置都是它可以被调到的某个尺度。这个词从人的行事方式，转到设备可重复的运行方式。

senses.title: A way to travel
senses.definition: a particular means or system of moving people or goods, such as rail, road, air, or water
senses.definitionCN: 运送人或货物的特定手段或系统，如铁路、公路、航空或水运
senses.example: Rail is still the cheapest mode of transport for coal.
senses.exampleCN: 对煤炭来说，铁路仍是最便宜的运输方式。
senses.why: Transport is measured out by the vehicle and the route chosen. The fixed phrase 'mode of transport' treats each means of travel as one measured option among several.
senses.whyCN: 运输由所选的交通工具与路线量定。固定短语“mode of transport”把每一种出行手段都当作若干被量定的选项之一。

senses.title: A way of producing
senses.definition: the organized way in which a society or economy makes goods, especially in economic and historical writing
senses.definitionCN: 社会或经济制造商品的有机组织方式，尤用于经济与历史写作
senses.example: The factory changed the mode of production from batch work to a moving line.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂把生产方式从分批作业改成了流水线。
senses.why: Economics borrowed the measure for the whole arrangement of work: tools, labour, and ownership fitted together into one measured pattern of making things.
senses.whyCN: 经济学借用了这个“尺度”，用来指整个劳动安排：工具、劳动力与所有权被合成一个被量定的制造格局。

senses.title: The prevailing fashion
senses.definition: the current fashion or style, especially in dress, in somewhat formal or old-fashioned use
senses.definitionCN: 当下的风尚或款式，尤指服饰，语气较正式或略显旧式
senses.example: Narrow coats were the mode in the winter of that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那年冬天，窄身大衣正是风尚。
senses.why: French mode means fashion, a specialized use of the same word. Fashion is the measure everyone agrees to wear for a season, so the sense of 'current style' grows straight out of 'measure'.
senses.whyCN: 法语 mode 意为“时尚”，是同一个词的专门用法。时尚就是大家在一季里共同同意穿着的尺度，所以“当下款式”这一义项直接从“尺度”长出来。

senses.title: A musical mode
senses.definition: a pattern of intervals used to organize a melody, especially one of the ancient or church modes
senses.definitionCN: 用来组织旋律的音程模式，尤指古代调式或教会调式
senses.example: The second movement is built on an old church mode rather than a major key.
senses.exampleCN: 第二乐章建立在古老的教会调式上，而不是大调上。
senses.why: Latin modus also meant rhythm and song. Musicians divide the octave by a measured pattern, and that pattern of intervals is literally the measure of the melody.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 modus 也指节奏与歌曲。音乐家按一种被量定的模式划分八度，这种音程模式字面上就是旋律的尺度。

senses.title: A grammatical mood
senses.definition: the form of a verb that shows whether it states, commands, wishes, or supposes
senses.definitionCN: 动词的形式，表明它是在陈述、命令、祝愿还是假设
senses.example: In Latin the verb's mode tells whether it states a fact or gives an order.
senses.exampleCN: 在拉丁语中，动词的语气表明它是在陈述事实还是下达命令。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word for the form that measures the speaker's attitude toward the action. Late Latin used modus for this category, and English kept it beside the more common 'mood'.
senses.whyCN: 语法学借用了这个词，指量定说话人对动作态度的形式。晚期拉丁语用 modus 指这一范畴，英语把它与更常见的 mood 并留着。

senses.title: The statistical mode
senses.definition: in statistics, the value that occurs most frequently in a set of data
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中在一组数据里出现次数最多的值
senses.example: In this data set the mode is 4, because 4 appears more often than any other value.
senses.exampleCN: 在这组数据中，众数是 4，因为 4 出现的次数比其他任何值都多。
senses.why: Statistics keeps the old sense of measure but points it at frequency: the mode is the value where the data pile up, the measure at which the set is most itself.
senses.whyCN: 统计学保留了这个词古老的“尺度”义，却把它指向频次：众数是数据堆积之处，是这组数据最像自己的那个尺度。

senses.title: A whole way of being
senses.definition: a general state or manner of existence, as in 'survival mode' or 'a mode of life'
senses.definitionCN: 总体的存在状态或生活方式，如“survival mode”或“a mode of life”
senses.example: During the storm the crew went into survival mode and stopped all repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨期间，船员进入求生模式，停止了所有修理。
senses.why: The measure can be applied to a whole life, not just one action. A mode of being is the overall pattern a person or group is currently cut to.
senses.whyCN: 这个尺度可以被用在整整一种生活上，而不只是一个动作。存在方式，就是一个人或群体当下被裁成的总体格局。

intro.en: Mode comes from Latin modus 'measure' through French, and the same measure runs through music, grammar, fashion, economics, and statistics. Its look-alike mood is a different word. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mode 经法语来自拉丁语 modus“尺度”，同一把尺子贯穿音乐、语法、时尚、经济与统计。与它形近的 mood 是另一个词。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Mode is first recorded in English meaning 'melodies, strains of music', a sense now obsolete. It came from Old French mode and directly from Latin modus.
items.cn: mode 在英语中最早记录为“旋律、乐曲”，这一义项今已废弃。它来自古法语 mode，并直接来自拉丁语 modus。

items.en: Latin modus meant 'measure, extent, quantity; proper measure, rhythm, song; a way, manner, fashion, style', and in Late Latin also 'mood' in grammar and logic.
items.cn: 拉丁语 modus 意为“尺度、范围、数量；恰当的尺度、节奏、歌曲；方式、做法、样式、风格”，在晚期拉丁语中还指语法与逻辑中的“语气”。

items.en: Modus goes back to PIE *med- 'take appropriate measures'. The same root lies behind moderate, modest, modify, model, modern, and medicine.
items.cn: modus 可追溯到原始印欧语 *med-“采取恰当的尺度”。同一词根也是 moderate、modest、modify、model、modern、medicine 的来源。

items.en: A second French borrowing gives mode the sense 'current fashion, prevailing style' (1640s). The central sense 'manner of acting or doing, the way in which a thing is done' is recorded by the 1660s.
items.cn: 另一次法语借入使 mode 获得“当下时尚、流行款式”之义（17 世纪 40 年代）。核心义“行事方式、做一件事的方式”到 17 世纪 60 年代才有记录。

items.en: The grammatical sense 'inflectional category in conjugation' is mid-15c. In music, mode is recorded from the 1670s for the Greek method of dividing the octave, and by 1721 for modern music.
items.cn: 语法义“变位中的屈折范畴”出现于 15 世纪中叶。音乐中，mode 于 17 世纪 70 年代指希腊人划分八度的方法，到 1721 年指现代音乐中的调式。

items.en: Mood 'state of mind' (c. 1300) comes from Old English mod 'heart, frame of mind', a word of unknown origin, and has no etymological link with mode. Grammatical mood (1570s) is a different word again: it is an alteration of mode.
items.cn: mood“心境”（约 1300）来自古英语 mod“心、心境”，词源不明，与 mode 没有词源关系。语法上的 mood（16 世纪 70 年代）又是另一个词：它是 mode 的变体拼写。

note.en: The first group separates mode from the look-alikes built on the same or a neighbouring stem; the second compares the ordinary words for 'the way something is done'.
note.cn: 第一组把 mode 与同词干或邻近词干的形近词分开；第二组比较表示“做事的方式”的常用词。

entries.tag: state of mind not from modus
entries.definition: a temporary state of mind or feeling. It comes from Old English mod, not from Latin modus. Only the grammatical mood is a different word, an alteration of mode.
entries.definitionCN: 暂时的心境或情绪。它来自古英语 mod，而不是拉丁语 modus。只有语法上的 mood 是另一个词，即 mode 的变体。

entries.definition: a small representation or an example to copy. It goes back to Latin modellus, a diminutive of modus, so it is 'a little measure' rather than a way of acting.
entries.definitionCN: 小型的代表物或供模仿的范例。它可追溯到拉丁语 modellus，即 modus 的指小形式，所以它是“一个小小的尺度”，而不是行事方式。

entries.definition: relating to mode, especially in grammar, music, or logic. It is the adjective; mode is the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 与 mode 有关的，尤用于语法、音乐或逻辑。它是形容词，mode 是名词。

entries.definition: fashionable, often with a hint of contempt. It is built from mode in its 'fashion' sense plus -ish.
entries.definitionCN: 时髦的，常带一丝轻蔑。它由表示“时尚”的 mode 加 -ish 构成。

entries.definition: a planned and organized procedure for doing something, often teachable step by step. A mode is the shape of the doing; a method is the route with steps.
entries.definitionCN: 为做某事而计划的、有组织的程序，通常可以一步步传授。mode 是做法呈现的形态，method 是带步骤的路线。

entries.definition: the way in which something is done, often with attention to style or bearing. It is close to mode but more personal and less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的方式，常带有风格或举止的意味。它接近 mode，但更个人化，技术性更弱。

entries.definition: the most general word for how something is done. It can replace mode in most everyday sentences, though not in fixed terms such as mode of production.
entries.definitionCN: 表示“如何做”的最通用词。它在多数日常句子里可以替换 mode，但不能替换 mode of production 这类固定说法。

entries.definition: a prevailing custom or style, and also 'in the manner of'. It overlaps with mode in the sense 'current style', but mode is far more formal there.
entries.definitionCN: 流行风俗或款式，也可表示“以……的方式”。它在“当下款式”一义上与 mode 重叠，但 mode 在该义上正式得多。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin modus 'measure', the PIE root *med-, and the English family modal, modality, model, and modify.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 modus“尺度”、原始印欧语词根 *med-，以及英语词族 modal、modality、model、modify。

normal.en: modus is Latin for 'measure'. A mode is the measure an action is cut to, which is why the word covers ways, settings, and styles at once.
normal.cn: modus 是拉丁语的“尺度”。mode 就是一个动作被裁成的尺寸，所以这个词同时覆盖方式、设置与款式。

normal.en: The fixed phrases keep the measure visible: mode of transport, mode of production, mode of operation.
normal.cn: 固定短语把“尺度”保留在明面上：交通方式、生产方式、运作方式。

normal.en: mood 'state of mind' is not related: it comes from Old English mod. Only grammatical mood is a variant of mode.
normal.cn: mood“心境”与它无关：它来自古英语 mod。只有语法上的 mood 才是 mode 的变体。

normal.en: model is a 'little measure' (Latin modellus), a pattern to copy, not a way of doing.
normal.cn: model 是“小小的尺度”（拉丁语 modellus），指供模仿的范本，而不是行事方式。

normal.en: modal, modality, and multimodal all keep the noun's stem; they describe the form or the channel, not the fashion.
normal.cn: modal、modality、multimodal 都保留了这个名词的词干；它们描述形式或通道，而不指时尚。

abstract.en: Picture a tailor's ruler laid on cloth. The ruler does not decide what the cloth is for; it only fixes the shape. Mode is that ruler applied to an action.
abstract.cn: 想象一把裁缝尺压在布上。尺子不决定布用来做什么，只固定形状。mode 就是那把量在动作上的尺子。

abstract.en: A switch with several positions is a row of modes: each position is a stable measure the machine can return to.
abstract.cn: 一个有多个挡位的开关就是一排模式：每个挡位都是机器可以回到的稳定尺度。

abstract.en: Fashion is a measure everyone agrees to wear for a season; that is why the same word can mean 'way' and 'style'.
abstract.cn: 时尚就是大家在一季里共同同意穿着的尺度；正因如此，同一个词既能指“方式”，又能指“款式”。

examples.en: The city's buses and trains are two modes of the same public transport system.
examples.cn: 城市的公交与地铁是同一套公共交通系统里的两种方式。

examples.en: Please leave the phone in silent mode during the examination.
examples.cn: 考试期间请把手机留在静音模式。

examples.en: The historian argues that a new mode of production changed the family as well as the factory.
examples.cn: 这位历史学家主张，新的生产方式不仅改变了工厂，也改变了家庭。

dict_mnemonic.text: “摸的”——先摸清门道，量好尺寸再动手，什么东西就按什么方式做 → mode 方式、模式（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 modus“尺度、方式”，核心是“按一把量好的尺子去做，形成固定的做法”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of mode, all cut from one measure: a ruler that fixes the shape of an action, a machine setting, a melody, a verb form, or a whole way of life.
sensesIntro.cn: mode 的九个义项都从同一把尺子上裁下：它固定一个动作、一个设备设置、一段旋律、一种动词形式或一整种生活形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler laid on something to fix its shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子压在事物上，固定它的形状。

branches.en: MEASURE APPLIED: a human action takes a shape, and a machine takes a repeatable setting.
branches.cn: 尺度落下：人的动作被定形，机器被调到一个可重复的设置。

branches.en: ORGANIZED MEANS: transport and production each settle into a measured arrangement of vehicles, tools, and labour.
branches.cn: 有组织的手段：运输与生产各自固定成由车辆、工具与劳动组成的被量定安排。

branches.en: STYLE AND SONG: the measure becomes the fashion of a season and the interval pattern of a melody.
branches.cn: 款式与歌曲：这把尺子变成一季的时尚，也变成旋律的音程模式。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: the verb's form is the measure of the speaker's attitude.
branches.cn: 语法：动词的形式成为说话人态度的尺度。

branches.en: DATA AND LIFE: the mode is where data pile up, and a mode of life is the whole pattern a person is cut to.
branches.cn: 数据与生活：众数是数据堆积之处，而生活方式是一个人被裁成的整体格局。

intro.en: Mode is a Latin noun, and mod- is one of the most productive stems in English: -al, -ality, -ish, -ern, -el, -ule, -ify and multi- all attach to it.
intro.cn: mode 是拉丁语名词，mod- 是英语里最能产出的词干之一：-al、-ality、-ish、-ern、-el、-ule、-ify 与 multi- 都能接在它上面。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is modus 'measure', with diminutives modulus and modellus and the verb moderari 'keep within measure'. All of them keep the idea of a fixed proportion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基是 modus“尺度”，另有指小形式 modulus 与 modellus，以及动词 moderari“保持在尺度之内”。它们都保留“固定比例”的意思。

items.meaningCN: 方式；模式（拉丁语“尺度、方式”）
items.example: The app has a simple mode for beginners.
items.exampleCN: 这个应用为初学者设有一个简单模式。

items.meaning: relating to mode, mood, or form
items.meaningCN: 模态的；语气的（mod- 尺度 + -al 形容词后缀）
items.example: The grammar lesson covers modal verbs such as 'can' and 'must'.
items.exampleCN: 这堂语法课讲 can、must 这类情态动词。

items.meaning: a mode or channel of something
items.meaningCN: 模态；形式；感觉通道（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: The study compares visual and auditory modalities.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究比较视觉与听觉通道。

items.meaningCN: 多模态的（multi- 多 + modal 模态的）
items.example: The course uses a multimodal approach with text, sound, and images.
items.exampleCN: 这门课采用文字、声音与图像的多模态方法。

items.meaningCN: 时髦的（mode 时尚 + -ish 形容词后缀）
items.example: The room was furnished in a modish style that dated quickly.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间按一种很快过时的时髦风格布置。

items.meaning: no longer in fashion or use
items.meaningCN: 过时的（out- 超出 + mode 款式 + -ed）
items.example: The factory still runs on outmoded equipment.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂仍在用过时的设备运转。

items.meaningCN: 模型；范本（mod- 尺度 + -el 指小后缀）
items.example: They built a scale model of the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 他们制作了这座桥的比例模型。

items.meaningCN: 现代的（-ern 构成形容词）
items.example: Modern offices rarely keep paper files.
items.exampleCN: 现代办公室很少保存纸质档案。

items.meaningCN: 适度的；使缓和（保持在应有尺度内）
items.example: The region has a moderate climate.
items.exampleCN: 这个地区气候温和。

items.meaning: to change in measure or detail
items.example: The engineers modified the valve to reduce flow.
items.exampleCN: 工程师改动了阀门以减少流量。

items.meaningCN: 模块；单元（mod- 尺度 + -ule 指小后缀）
items.example: The software is built from reusable modules.
items.exampleCN: 这个软件由可复用的模块构成。

items.meaning: to adjust in measure, tone, or strength
items.meaningCN: 调节；调制（按小尺度调整）
items.example: She modulated her voice so as not to wake the baby.
items.exampleCN: 她压低并调节了声音，以免吵醒婴儿。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 小尺度；范本（modus 的指小形式）

definition_zh: 盛行；普遍存在；占上风；获胜；说服
definition_en: to be widespread or dominant, to win out over opposition, or to persuade someone to act
core_image: 山口的风整日不停，一面旧旗被吹得贴住旗杆，却始终没有倒下
scene: 山口的风整日不停，一面旧旗被吹得贴住旗杆，却始终没有倒下。 Westerly winds prevail over the pass for most of the year.
sceneCN: 这里指风与天气长期占主导（第 1 个义项：风与天气盛行）；句意为西风一年中大部分时间控制着这个山口。图中可辨识物件：山口、旧旗、旗杆、被风压弯的草；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 盛行；普遍存在；占上风；获胜；说服

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加形容词词尾构成，义为「盛行的；普遍的」
由「盛行」的形容词加名词尾构成，义为「盛行；普遍程度」
由该动词加形容词词尾构成，义为「占优势的；盛行的」
由「占优势的」形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「占优势地」
与拉丁语「valere」同族，经法语进入英语，义为「有用；有帮助」

senses.title: Of wind and weather
senses.definition: to blow steadily or to be the usual weather of a place and season
senses.definitionCN: 指风持续地吹，或成为某地某季的常况
senses.example: Dry winds prevail across the plateau in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬季高原上盛行干燥的风。
senses.why: The earliest English uses describe forces that hold the air, because prevailing is first about what dominates a place.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的用法描述控制空气的力量，因为「盛行」首先指在某地占主导。

senses.title: Of customs and ideas
senses.definition: to be widely found or generally accepted among a group of people
senses.definitionCN: 在一群人中广泛存在或被普遍接受
senses.example: The custom still prevails in the mountain villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗在山村里仍然盛行。
senses.why: Once a usage holds a region the way weather does, the verb extends from air to habit.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一种做法像天气那样占住一个地区，这个动词就从空气扩展到习惯。

senses.title: To win an argument
senses.definition: to prove stronger than the opposing case in a debate or dispute
senses.definitionCN: 在辩论或争执中证明比对方的主张更强
senses.example: Common sense prevailed after a long debate.
senses.exampleCN: 经过长时间辩论，常理占了上风。
senses.why: Being stronger is the core of the Latin verb, and an argument is a contest of strength between claims.
senses.whyCN: 「更强」是拉丁动词的核心，而争论正是各种主张之间的力量较量。

senses.title: To win a contest
senses.definition: to defeat opponents in a match, a race or a struggle
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、竞速或斗争中击败对手
senses.example: The home side prevailed in the final minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 主队在最后几分钟取胜。
senses.why: Sport borrowed the legal and military verb for the side that turns out stronger.
senses.whyCN: 体育界借用了这个法律与军事动词，指最终更强的一方。

senses.title: To persuade someone
senses.definition: to bring someone round to a course of action by argument or appeal
senses.definitionCN: 通过论证或请求使某人接受某种做法
senses.example: She prevailed on the committee to reopen the case.
senses.exampleCN: 她说服委员会重新审理此案。
senses.why: Persuasion is winning a person over, so the preposition on marks the one who is overcome.
senses.whyCN: 说服就是把一个人争取过来，因此搭配的介词标出被说服的那一方。

senses.title: Of effort that succeeds at last
senses.definition: to succeed after sustained pressure, patience or repeated attempts
senses.definitionCN: 在持续施压、耐心等待或反复尝试之后取得成功
senses.example: Patience and evidence finally prevailed.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心与证据最终奏效。
senses.why: The verb can name an impersonal force that wins, even when no person is doing the winning.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以指一种非人的力量取胜，即使并没有人在取胜。

senses.title: Of an old rule that outlives its reason
senses.titleCN: 旧制度延续而缘由已失
senses.definition: to remain in force long after the purpose it once served has disappeared
senses.definitionCN: 在当初的用途消失很久之后仍然有效
senses.example: The old rule still prevails long after its purpose vanished.
senses.exampleCN: 那条旧规定在用途消失很久后仍然有效。
senses.why: What prevails simply holds its ground, whether or not anyone can still explain why.
senses.whyCN: 「盛行」的东西只是守住自己的位置，不管还有没有人能解释缘由。

senses.title: To win in a court of law
senses.definition: to succeed in a legal action or to establish a right against the other party
senses.definitionCN: 在法律诉讼中成功，或对另一方确立一项权利
senses.example: The tenant prevailed in the housing dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 租户在住房纠纷中胜诉。
senses.why: Legal language keeps the old sense of a stronger claim carrying the day.
senses.whyCN: 法律语言保留了旧义，即更强的主张最终获胜。

intro.en: Prevail comes from Latin prae-, before or beyond, and valere, to be strong or to be worth, forming praevalere, to be stronger. English took it through French in the fourteenth century; the family of valere also includes valid, value and avail.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语前缀「prae-」「在前、超出」与「valere」「强、有价值」，合成「praevalere」「更强」。英语于十四世纪经法语引入；「valere」的同族词还包括「valid」「value」「avail」。

items.en: Valere meant to be strong or to be worth, and it described health, power and value alike.
items.cn: 这个词意为强壮或有价值，同时描述健康、力量与价值。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or beyond, marking a position ahead of others.
items.cn: 前缀意为「在前」或「超出」，标出比别人更靠前的位置。

items.en: Prae plus valere gave praevalere, to be stronger, whose past stem is praevaluī.
items.cn: 前缀加动词得到「praevalere」「更强」，其过去词干为「praevaluī」。

items.en: Old French carried the verb to English, where it was spelled and pronounced in several ways before settling.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带到英语，其拼写与读音经过几种形式才固定下来。

items.en: English used prevail first for holding power or influence, and soon for winning a contest.
items.cn: 英语最初用这个词表示掌握权力或影响力，很快也用于表示在较量中获胜。

items.en: Courts fixed the sense of winning a case, while ordinary speech kept the weather, custom and persuasion senses.
items.cn: 法庭固定了「胜诉」义，而日常口语保留了天气、习俗与说服诸义。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like prevail; the second group names neighbouring ideas of dominance, victory and persuasion.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「prevail」相近；第二组是与「支配、取胜、说服」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective for what is dominant or most common, as in the prevailing wind.
entries.definitionCN: 指占主导或最常见的形容词，如盛行风。

entries.definition: Widespread in a place or at a time, often used of diseases or beliefs.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某地某时广泛存在的，常用于疾病或观念。

entries.definition: The fact or degree of being widespread.
entries.definitionCN: 指广泛存在的事实或程度。

entries.definition: To be useful or helpful; it shares the Latin strength word.
entries.definitionCN: 指有用、有帮助；共用同一个拉丁「强」词。

entries.definition: Bravery in battle, from the same Latin word for strength.
entries.definitionCN: 指战斗中的勇猛，出自同一个表示力量的拉丁词。

entries.definition: To hold the most power or influence in a place or situation.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某地或某种情境中掌握最大的权力或影响。

entries.definition: To be the largest or most noticeable element among others.
entries.definitionCN: 指在其他要素中数量最多或最显著。

entries.definition: To win a decisive victory, often with a sense of celebration.
entries.definitionCN: 指取得决定性胜利，常带庆祝意味。

entries.definition: To convince someone to believe or do something.
entries.definitionCN: 指说服某人相信或去做某事。

entries.definition: To continue in existence or action, close to the sense of an old rule still holding.
entries.definitionCN: 指继续存在或继续行动，接近旧规定仍然有效那一义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin strength word behind prevail, its real family and its fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个词背后表示「强」的拉丁词、真实同族词与固定搭配。

normal.en: Praemia and prevail share a Latin idea: the stronger thing stands, and the stronger claim wins.
normal.cn: 奖品与盛行共享一个拉丁观念：更强的东西站住，更强的主张获胜。

normal.en: The prefix means before or beyond, and the stem means strong, so prevail is to be stronger than what stands in front.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「在前、超出」，词干意为「强」，所以这个词指比挡在前面的东西更强。

normal.en: Prevail on someone is the fixed pattern for persuasion, with the preposition on before the person.
normal.cn: 劝说某人用的是固定模式，介词放在人前面。

normal.en: The prevailing wind is the weather phrase, and it is the oldest kind of use.
normal.cn: 盛行风是天气方面的说法，也是最古老的一类用法。

normal.en: Valid, value and avail all descend from the same Latin word for being strong or worth something.
normal.cn: 有效的、价值与有用都出自同一个表示「强或有价值」的拉丁词。

abstract.en: Prevailing is not shouting loudest; it is being the thing that is still standing when the wind drops.
abstract.cn: 盛行不是喊得最响，而是风停之后仍然立着的那一个。

abstract.en: An old rule prevails because nobody remembers how to remove it, not because it is right.
abstract.cn: 旧规定之所以延续，是因为没人记得怎样废除它，而不是因为它正确。

abstract.en: To prevail is to make the world agree with you without having to raise your voice.
abstract.cn: 占上风是让世界同意你，而不必提高嗓门。

examples.en: Cooler air will prevail over the region by the weekend.
examples.cn: 到周末，较凉的空气将控制这一地区。

examples.en: The older interpretation prevailed among historians for a century.
examples.cn: 较旧的解释在历史学家中盛行了整整一个世纪。

examples.en: They tried to prevail on the minister to change the policy.
examples.cn: 他们试图说服部长改变这项政策。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普瑞威尔」——「普」遍都「瑞」气「威」风，处处占上风：盛行、取胜、说服。

root: 拉丁语「prae-」「在前、超出」加「valere」「强、有价值」构成「praevalere」「更强」，其过去词干为「praevaluī」；英语十四世纪经法语引入；「valere」同族有「valid」「value」「avail」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from wind holding a place, to a custom being widespread, an argument or contest won, a person persuaded, effort succeeding, an old rule surviving, and a case won in law.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从风占住一地，走向习俗广布、争论或较量取胜、说服某人、努力奏效、旧制度延续，以及法律上胜诉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flag that bends in a steady gale but never falls, because the stronger force holds its ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面旗在稳定的大风里被压弯却从不倒下，因为更强的力量守住了位置。

branches.en: THE WEATHER: one wind or one kind of weather holds a place for most of the year.
branches.cn: 天气：一种风或一类天气在一年的大部分时间里占住一个地方。

branches.en: THE LONG HABIT: a custom spreads widely, and an old rule stays after its reason is gone.
branches.cn: 长久的习惯：习俗广泛流传，旧规定在缘由消失后仍留下。

branches.en: THE STRONGER CLAIM: an argument wins out, and a side wins the match.
branches.cn: 更强的主张：一种论点占上风，一方赢下比赛。

branches.en: THE OVERCOMING: a person is persuaded, and patient effort succeeds at last.
branches.cn: 争取与奏效：一个人被说服，耐心的努力最终成功。

branches.en: THE COURT: the stronger legal right carries the case.
branches.cn: 法庭：更强的法律权利赢得案件。

intro.en: Prevail is a Latin verb built from a prefix of position and a stem of strength, and English keeps both pieces in a whole family.
intro.cn: 这是一个由位置前缀与力量词干构成的拉丁动词，英语在两个成分上都保留了一整族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere supplies the strength, prae- supplies the advantage, and praevalere joins them into one verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「valere」提供力量，「prae-」提供优势，「praevalere」把两者合成一个动词。

definition_zh: 市场经济；由价格与私人自愿交易配置资源的经济体制；与计划经济相对的经济形态
definition_en: an economic system in which prices, private ownership and voluntary exchange, rather than central directives, decide what is produced and how resources are allocated
core_image: 天没亮的集市：摊主各自写价牌，买主来回比价，没有谁在高处统一派货，价钱随人流涨落
scene: 一个城镇的早市在天还没亮时开张，摊主各自标价，买主挑拣还价，收摊时谁的货卖得动、谁的要剩下一半，全由当天的价钱决定。 In a market economy, no office sets the price of bread; buyers and sellers do.
sceneCN: 早市里没有统一发号施令的人，价格由买卖双方当场议定，货物也随之流向愿出价的一方。句中的 market economy 指「由价格与私人交易配置资源的经济形态」（第 1 个义项：价格信号而非行政指令决定生产与分配）。图中可辨识物件：手写价牌、秤、零钱盒、半空的货筐。

pos.zh: 市场经济（指一种经济体制，通常作不可数；指多个经济体时可用复数）

collocations.phrase: the rise of the market economy

senses.title: Prices, not orders, allocate resources
senses.titleCN: 由价格而非指令配置资源的经济体制
senses.definition: an economic order in which relative prices guide what gets produced and who gets the output
senses.definitionCN: 一种经济秩序，其中相对价格引导生产什么、产出归谁
senses.example: In a market economy, a shortage of copper shows up as a higher price rather than as a queue.
senses.exampleCN: 在市场经济中，铜的短缺表现为价格上涨，而不是排队。
senses.why: market names the arena of buying and selling, and economy names the management of a household's resources; joined, they say that the arena itself does the managing.
senses.whyCN: market 指买卖的场所，economy 指对家计资源的管理；两者相接，等于说「管理」这件事由买卖场所本身来完成。

senses.title: Private ownership as the default
senses.titleCN: 以私人产权为默认前提的经济
senses.definition: an economy in which the means of production are mostly held privately and can be bought or sold
senses.definitionCN: 生产资料主要由私人持有、可以买卖的经济
senses.example: A market economy presupposes that factories and farmland have owners who may sell them.
senses.exampleCN: 市场经济的前提是工厂与农田有可以出售它们的所有者。
senses.why: exchange requires something exchangeable, so the phrase carries private title to productive assets as part of its meaning rather than as an afterthought.
senses.whyCN: 交换需要可交换之物，因此这个短语把生产性资产的私人所有权当作自身含义的一部分，而非附加条件。

senses.title: The destination of post-socialist reform
senses.titleCN: 转轨国家改革的目标形态
senses.definition: the endpoint that former command economies were said to be moving toward after price controls were lifted
senses.definitionCN: 价格管制解除后，原指令型经济体被称说正在走向的终点
senses.example: The country declared its intention to build a market economy within ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 该国宣布打算在十年内建成市场经济。
senses.why: the phrase became a programme in the late twentieth century, when it named not a description but a direction of travel for states leaving central planning.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪后期，这个短语成了一个纲领：它不再描述现状，而是给离开中央计划的国家指出方向。

senses.title: A legal status in trade disputes
senses.titleCN: 贸易争端中的法律地位认定
senses.definition: a finding that a country's prices and costs are set by the market, which affects how anti-dumping duties are calculated
senses.definitionCN: 认定一国的价格与成本由市场决定，从而影响反倾销税的计算方式
senses.example: The exporters argued that their home market was a market economy and that domestic prices should be used as the benchmark.
senses.exampleCN: 出口商主张其国内市场属于市场经济，应以国内价格作为基准。
senses.why: trade law turned the abstract phrase into a testable label, because the benchmark used in duty calculations depends on whether prices are market-determined.
senses.whyCN: 贸易法把这个抽象短语变成一个可认定的标签，因为计税基准取决于价格是否由市场决定。

senses.title: The market-run half of a mixed system
senses.titleCN: 混合体制中以市场运作的那一部分
senses.definition: the portion of a mixed system in which firms trade freely, as distinct from the state-run portion
senses.definitionCN: 混合体制中企业与市场自由交易的部分，与国营部分相区别
senses.example: Even in a mixed system, the market economy covers most retail trade and nearly all farming.
senses.exampleCN: 即使在混合体制中，市场经济也覆盖了大部分零售与几乎所有农业。
senses.why: the same phrase can be read partitively, naming a slice of an economy rather than the whole of it, which is why it appears beside state sectors.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语也可作部分读，指一个经济体中被市场运作的一块，而非整体，因此它会与国营部门并提。

senses.title: A political label for capitalism
senses.titleCN: 政治话语中对资本主义秩序的代称
senses.definition: a rhetorical name for a capitalist order, used to praise or to attack it rather than to describe it neutrally
senses.definitionCN: 对资本主义秩序的一种修辞性称呼，用于褒扬或攻击，而非中立描述
senses.example: The speech praised the market economy as the only road to prosperity.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲称赞市场经济是通往繁荣的唯一道路。
senses.why: once the phrase entered political argument it acquired a tone, so speakers use it to signal approval of private enterprise or to name an opponent.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语一旦进入政治论辩便带上了色彩：说话者用它表示赞同私营企业，或用来指称对手。

senses.title: A reform package of liberalisation steps
senses.titleCN: 由自由化措施组成的改革方案
senses.definition: the bundle of measures, such as price liberalisation, privatisation and subsidy cuts, that are meant to create such a system
senses.definitionCN: 价格放开、私有化、削减补贴等一整套旨在建立该体制的措施
senses.example: Building a market economy required freeing prices, selling state plants and ending cheap credit.
senses.exampleCN: 建立市场经济需要放开价格、出售国营工厂并停止廉价信贷。
senses.why: because the phrase named a goal, it came to stand for the steps taken toward it, and that bundle is now what officials mean by the term.
senses.whyCN: 因为短语指称一个目标，它也渐渐指称通往目标所采取的步骤，官员说到这个词时指的往往就是那套措施。

senses.title: An ideal type in economic theory
senses.titleCN: 经济理论中的理想类型
senses.definition: an analytical model in which all allocation is assumed to run through prices, with institutions and politics abstracted away
senses.definitionCN: 一种分析模型，假设全部配置都经价格进行，把制度与政治抽象掉
senses.example: The textbook treats a market economy as a model in which every actor responds to the same price signal.
senses.exampleCN: 教科书把市场经济当作一个所有行动者都对同一价格信号作出反应的模型。
senses.why: theory needs a clean benchmark, so the phrase also names a simplified construct rather than any observable country.
senses.whyCN: 理论需要一个干净的基准，因此这个短语也指一个简化的构造，而非任何可观察的国家。

intro.en: Market economy joins two borrowings: market goes back to Latin mercatus, the noun of trading, while economy goes back to Greek oikonomia, the management of a household, which reached English through Latin oeconomia. The compound itself is a twentieth-century term of political economy.
intro.cn: market economy 由两个借词拼成：market 出自拉丁 mercatus「交易、市场」，economy 出自希腊 oikonomia「家计管理」，后者经拉丁 oeconomia 进入英语。短语本身是二十世纪政治经济学的术语。

items.en: Mercatus meant a market and the business done there. It came from the verb mercari 'to trade', which in turn rests on the noun merx (genitive mercis) 'goods, merchandise'. The deeper origin of merx is uncertain, and any older form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: mercatus 指市场以及在那里进行的买卖，出自动词 mercari「做买卖」，而该动词又基于名词 merx（属格 mercis）「货物」。merx 的更早来源不确定，凡为其提出的更古形式均属重构形式。

items.en: Mercari 'to buy and sell' supplied mercatus, which passed through Old North French into English as market, first naming a place of trade and later the demand for a good.
items.cn: mercari「买卖」提供了 mercatus，后者经古北法语进入英语作 market，最初指交易场所，后来也指对某种货物的需求。

items.en: Oikonomia combined oikos 'house, household' with nemein 'to distribute, to manage', so it named the running of a household and its stores. The deeper history of nemein is debated, and proposed Indo-European links are reconstructions.
items.cn: oikonomia 由 oikos「家宅」与 nemein「分配、管理」合成，指料理家宅与家中储备。nemein 的更早历史有争论，所提出的印欧语关联属重构形式。

items.en: Latin took the Greek word as oeconomia. English economy entered in the sixteenth century meaning household management, and by the eighteenth century it meant the ordered system of a state's wealth and production.
items.cn: 拉丁语以 oeconomia 借入这个希腊词。英语 economy 于十六世纪进入，意为家计管理；到十八世纪，它指一国财富与生产的有序体系。

items.en: The full phrase was coined in the twentieth century as the counterpart of planned economy and command economy, and it became standard in development policy and in comparisons of economic systems.
items.cn: 完整短语在二十世纪被造出，作为「计划经济」「指令经济」的对应说法，随后在发展政策与各种经济体制比较中成为标准用语。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of merx and the early sense of nemein are unsettled, and no single first citation for the English compound is established, so an earlier date sometimes given is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：merx 在拉丁语之前的来源与 nemein 的早期含义均无定论，英语复合短语也没有公认的最早书证，因此有时给出的更早年代属于重构。

note.en: Group one holds phrases that share a word with the target and are routinely mistaken for it; group two holds systems that lie close in meaning but differ over who owns the assets and who does the deciding.
note.cn: 第一组是与目标短语共用某个词、因而常被混用的说法；第二组是含义相近、但在「谁拥有资产」与「谁作决定」上不同的体制。

entries.definition: The name of an academic field that studies how markets behave; a country cannot build it, and it is not the economy itself.
entries.definitionCN: 一门研究市场如何运作的学科名称；国家无法「建成」它，它也不是经济本身。

entries.definition: The act of making a service or asset run through markets, such as housing or electricity; it names a change, whereas the target names a settled order.
entries.definitionCN: 把某项服务或资产改为经市场运作的过程，如住房或电力；它指变化，而目标词指一种成形秩序。

entries.definition: The square or website where trade happens; it is only the arena, not the ownership and legal order around it.
entries.definitionCN: 买卖发生的广场或网站；它只是场所，不含围绕它的产权与法律秩序。

entries.definition: A market left almost alone by the state; a market economy may still be heavily regulated, so the two are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎不受国家干预的市场；市场经济仍可受到严格监管，因此两者不能互换。

entries.definition: Names the system by who owns the assets rather than by how prices coordinate, shifting the emphasis onto property.
entries.definitionCN: 按「谁拥有资产」而非「价格如何协调」来命名该体制，重点落在产权上。

entries.definition: A system in which state and market sectors coexist; it is the ordinary compromise, not the textbook model.
entries.definitionCN: 国家部门与市场部门并存的经济体制；它是常见的折中形态，而非教科书模型。

entries.definition: Names just the network of prices that carries information; it says nothing about ownership, law or policy.
entries.definitionCN: 只指传递信息的整套价格；它对产权、法律与政策不置一词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real components, real fixed phrases and real historical contrast, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实的历史对立，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Market goes back to Latin mercatus 'a place of trading', which rests on merx 'goods': the word for the goods also gave the word for the place.
normal.cn: market 上溯拉丁 mercatus「交易场所」，而它基于 merx「货物」：指货物的词同时也给出了指场所的词。

normal.en: Economy goes back to Greek oikonomia, oikos 'house' plus nemein 'to manage': the word began as the running of a household.
normal.cn: economy 上溯希腊 oikonomia，由 oikos「家宅」与 nemein「管理」构成：这个词最初指料理家计。

normal.en: The phrase was built as the opposite of planned economy, so it always drags a comparison along with it.
normal.cn: 这个短语是作为「计划经济」的对立面造出的，因此它总带着一层比较的意味。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the reform sense: transition to a market economy, market economy status, market economy reforms.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出改革义：向市场经济过渡、市场经济地位、市场经济改革。

normal.en: Market also names demand itself, as in a market for used cars, which ties the arena to the appetite behind it.
normal.cn: market 也指需求本身，如二手车市场，这把「场所」与背后的需求连在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a town where every stall writes its own price and nobody in an office upstairs issues a quota.
abstract.cn: 想象一个镇上每个摊位自己写价，楼上没有哪间办公室在派定额。

abstract.en: Picture a household budget enlarged to the size of a country: that is the household word hidden inside economy.
abstract.cn: 想象一本家用的账本被放大到一国的规模：这就是藏在 economy 里的那个「家」字。

abstract.en: Picture two diagrams side by side, one with arrows from a centre and one with arrows between traders; the phrase names the second.
abstract.cn: 想象两张并排的图：一张箭头从中心发出，一张箭头在买卖者之间穿梭；这个短语指的是后一张。

examples.en: A market economy allocates goods through prices that move as supply and demand change.
examples.cn: 市场经济通过随供求变化而变动的价格来配置货物。

examples.en: After the price controls were lifted, the country moved toward a market economy within a decade.
examples.cn: 价格管制取消后，该国在十年内走向市场经济。

examples.en: Compared with a planned system, a market economy differs less in technology than in who may set a price.
examples.cn: 与计划体制相比，市场经济的差别不在技术，而在谁有权定价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「market（集市）+ economy（经济）」——摊位自己写价、买卖自己成交，一整国的买卖都照集市的样子运转，就是市场经济。

root: 拉丁 mercatus「市场、交易」← 动词 mercari「做买卖」← 名词 merx（属格 mercis）「货物」；希腊 oikonomia「家计管理」= oikos「家宅」+ nemein「分配、管理」，经拉丁 oeconomia 入英语；短语为二十世纪政治经济学术语，与计划经济相对。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one picture: an arena that sets its own prices is scaled up until it runs a whole economy, and that picture is then turned into a reform goal, a legal label, a sector, a slogan, a policy bundle and finally a textbook model.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个画面辐射开来：一个自己定价的买卖场所被放大到能运转整个经济体，这个画面随后被依次当作改革目标、法律标签、部门、口号、政策组合，最后成为教科书模型。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a morning market where each stall posts a price and the crowd, not an office, decides what sells.
core.cn: 核心意象：清早的集市，每个摊位自己挂牌，决定货物卖不卖得动的是人流，而不是哪间办公室。

branches.en: MARKET AS MANAGER: the arena takes over the household's job, and it can only do so if the assets have owners who may sell.
branches.cn: 市场当家：买卖场所接管了「理家」的活，而它要能做到这一点，资产必须有可以出售的所有者。

branches.en: FROM GOAL TO LABEL: leaving central planning turns the phrase into a destination, and trade law turns it into a status to be granted or refused.
branches.cn: 从目标到标签：离开中央计划使这个短语成为终点，贸易法则使它成为一项可授予也可拒绝的地位。

branches.en: PART AND SLOGAN: the same words can name one sector of a mixed system or serve as a flag in political argument.
branches.cn: 部分与口号：同一串词既可指混合体制中的一个部门，也可在政治论辩中充当旗帜。

branches.en: THE STEPS: because the phrase named a goal, it came to mean the liberalising measures taken to reach it.
branches.cn: 步骤：因为短语指称目标，它也转而指为达到目标而采取的自由化措施。

branches.en: THE MODEL: theory strips away law and politics to leave a benchmark in which price alone coordinates.
branches.cn: 模型：理论剥去法律与政治，只留下一个仅由价格协调的基准。

intro.en: The phrase can be read as two morpheme chains: a Latin root for trade that supplies market and its family, and a Greek compound for household management that supplies economy and its family.
intro.cn: 这个短语可以按两条语素链读：一条是拉丁的「交易」词根，提供 market 及其词族；一条是希腊的「家计管理」复合词，提供 economy 及其词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin merx and mercari give market, merchant and commerce; Greek oikos and nemein, taken into Latin as oeconomia, give economy, economic and economist.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 merx 与 mercari 衍生 market、merchant 与 commerce；希腊 oikos 与 nemein 经拉丁 oeconomia 衍生 economy、economic 与 economist。

items.example: Nemein supplies the managing half of the compound.

items.example: Nemein plus the suffix produces the abstract noun.

intro.en: Effectual comes from Latin efficere, to work out, through the participle effectus, a thing worked out; the suffix -ual says able to produce that result.
intro.cn: effectual 来自拉丁语 efficere（做出、促成），经由分词 effectus（做出来的东西，即结果）；后缀 -ual 表示「能产生那个结果的」。

items.en: Latin efficere means to work out or bring about, from ex- plus facere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 efficere 意为做出、促成，由 ex- 加 facere 构成。

items.en: The participle effectus names a thing worked out, a result.
items.cn: 分词 effectus 指做出来的东西，即结果。

items.en: Medieval Latin added -alis to build effectualis, able to produce a result.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语加 -alis 构成 effectualis，意为能产生结果的。

items.en: English took effectual in the 14C for a prayer or remedy that truly worked.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借用 effectual，指真正起作用的祷告或药方。

items.en: Lawyers used effectual for a deed or statute that carried binding force.
items.cn: 律师用 effectual 指有约束力的契据或法令。

items.en: Effective became the everyday word and effectual kept a formal, older tone.
items.cn: effective 成为日常用词，effectual 保留了较正式、较古旧的语气。

note.en: Effectual, effective and effectuate all grow from Latin facere, to make; the endings tell you whether the word names a quality, an adverb or an action.
note.cn: effectual、effective 与 effectuate 都源于拉丁语 facere（做）；词尾告诉你它指的是性质、方式还是动作。

dict_mnemonic.text: effectual ＝ ef-（向外，ex- 的变体）＋ fect（做，拉丁 facere）＋ -ual（形容词后缀，能…的）＝「能做出结果的」。同一条拉丁词根按词尾分家：-us → effect 结果；-ive → effective 有效的（日常首选）；-ual → effectual 奏效的（偏正式、偏古旧，也用于法律「有效的」）；-ually → effectually 奏效地；-uate → effectuate 使生效。想说「这药有效」日常用 effective 或 works，effectual 多出现在旧文献、法律文本与宗教写作里。注意与 efficient（有效率的，强调少浪费）区分：effectual 只看结果有没有出来，efficient 还看花了多少力气。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）＋ facere（做）→ efficere（促成）→ effectus（结果）→ effectual（奏效的）
